title: John Rich warns Nashville's famed Broadway could go dark as businesses face tax ‘death nail’
summary: John Rich warns Nashville's Lower Broadway honky-tonks face closure as property tax bills soar, threatening the live music culture that defines Music City.
story: Country music star John Rich told Fox News Digital that soaring property appraisals and higher taxes could force longtime businesses on Nashville’s famed Broadway to "turn out the lights."

Country star John Rich is warning that Nashville’s Lower Broadway, the iconic entertainment district famous for its glowing neon signs, packed honky-tonks and live country music, could soon begin going dark.

In a video that Rich shared on Facebook last week, the 52-year-old Big & Rich member sounded the alarm, declaring that "the lights are going out on Broadway" as Nashville businesses struggle under mounting property tax bills.

Speaking to Fox News Digital, Rich, who owns Redneck Riviera Bar & BBQ on Lower Broadway, argued that sharply higher property assessments along with increased taxes have pushed longtime Broadway establishments to a breaking point, which he said threatened not only the businesses themselves but the live music culture that earned Nashville its "Music City" nickname.

"It was a one-two punch," Rich said. "So the first thing he did was they reappraised everybody's property in the county, in the city, and as soon as they got that done, which was an extremely inflated appraisal rate, then they come in and raise the taxes aggressively on top of these extremely inflated appraisals."
COUNTRY STAR JOHN RICH JOINS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ADVOCATING FOR LANDOWNERS' RIGHTS
John Rich of Big & Rich warned that Nashville's famed Broadway could go dark due to soaring property assessments along with increased taxes. (Getty Images)

"And with those two things, what you've done is you've now put a death nail in a vast majority of the businesses," he continued. "It's only a matter of time before you're going to see large percentages of the businesses downtown turning out the lights."
"We've already had three in the past two weeks have to shut down. I'm talking major, major, major places that have been there for decades," Rich added.

Though Rich blamed Nashville Mayor Freddie O’Connell for the overall tax burden, the city's regularly scheduled four-year reappraisal, which took place in 2025, was conducted by the independently elected Davidson County assessor of property.
WATCH: JOHN RICH WARNS TAX ‘ONE-TWO PUNCH’ THREATENS BROADWAY

The 2025 reappraisal resulted in a 45% median increase in property values countywide. Under Tennessee law, the reappraisal itself is revenue-neutral, meaning the tax rate is adjusted so higher property values don't automatically generate additional revenue for local government.

However, O’Connell and the Metro Council subsequently set the Urban Services District tax rate at $2.814 per $100 of assessed value, 26% above the revenue-neutral certified rate, according to the assessor’s office.

The increases were particularly steep on Lower Broadway, where a 400% increase in real estate values was common, according to a report by Axios Nashville. The outlet also reported that many honky-tonk operators rent their buildings and are responsible for the property taxes under their leases, leaving them to shoulder rising tax bills without benefiting from the increased equity in the properties.
Rich warned that the establishments might have to charge "$50 a beer." (Jason Kempin)
Rich pointed to several Lower Broadway establishments while describing what he sees as a broader threat to businesses in the district.

He cited Nashville Underground, which permanently closed in May after roughly eight years in business, and Acme Feed & Seed, whose owner, Tom Morales, has warned it could close amid a steep increase in its property tax bill. Rich also said he has heard Hard Rock Cafe Nashville, a Broadway fixture since 1994, is considering closing, though Fox News Digital has not independently confirmed that claim.

Acme Feed & Seed, in particular, has emerged as a flashpoint in the debate over the rising tax burden. In February, Morales said the popular four-story restaurant, bar and live music venue's annual property tax bill had jumped from $129,000 to nearly $600,000.

Morales told Nashville's NewsChannel 5 that Acme Feed & Seed ended 2025 about $500,000 "in the red," while he and his daughter Lauren Morales later told the Nashville Scene that closure was "imminent" if they could not find a solution to the tax increase.
O’Connell addressed Morales' warnings at the time during an interview with Nashville's Fox 17.
"It’s not up to me whether he keeps that business open," O’Connell told the outlet. "The market evolves. New businesses start even as beloved old businesses close."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Rich expressed his concerns regarding the Super Bowl. (Jason Kempin)

The comments drew criticism, including from Metro Councilmember Jacob Kupin, who told Fox 17 he was "appalled" by the mayor's response. O’Connell’s office later accused the station of selectively editing and misrepresenting his remarks and released a longer version of the exchange.

In the fuller answer, O’Connell said the state comptroller had reviewed downtown valuations and determined they reflected market value. He called Acme's location "an incredibly valuable piece of property" and said it was up to the owner to determine how to capture that value.
Rich argued that Acme’s concerns are far from isolated, pointing to a recent meeting he attended with other Lower Broadway business owners.

"Then we had this meeting with all the business owners down there," Rich told Fox News Digital. "And in that meeting, all the ownership of Broadway was represented down there, and every single person said it's only a matter of time before we literally have to just close the doors because we're running at a deficit."
"We'd have to charge $50 a beer, which you can't do that," he continued. "I mean, there is no business model that exists that allows the businesses down there to stay open."
WATCH: JOHN RICH SAYS NASHVILLE BARS WOULD NEED TO CHARGE ‘$50 A BEER' TO SURVIVE
Rich emphasized that the bar and restaurant operators sounding the alarm include some of the most experienced in the city.
"You're not talking about a bunch of amateurs here," he said. "You're looking at the best of the best, and they can't survive it."
For Rich, however, the bigger concern is what the financial pressure could ultimately mean for Nashville’s identity.
"The bigger story to me is live music in Nashville. I mean, it's called Music City," he said.
Rich described the unique concentration of live music along Broadway, where honky-tonks line both sides of the street and bands perform throughout the day and into the early morning hours.

"You walk down Broadway, the doors are all open to all the honky-tonks, you're hearing music from the right side of your head and the left side of your head for five blocks in a row," Rich said. "There's 60, 70, 80 live music venues in that one concentration. It's the only place like it in the world."

"The French Quarter doesn't have that. Las Vegas doesn't have that. Times Square doesn't have that," he continued. "There's nowhere in America that has what downtown Nashville has when it comes to live music. And it is absolutely under threat."
Rich painted a dire picture of what he fears the entertainment district could eventually look like when Nashville hosts the 2030 Super Bowl.

"Can you imagine when the Super Bowl comes to Nashville here in a few years, and everybody's packed in on Broadway and there's only 30 or 40% of the neon signs that are even still lit up, if you're lucky?" he said. "That's what you're looking at happening. I mean, what a travesty that would be."

Rich, an outspoken conservative and longtime supporter of President Donald Trump, placed much of the blame for the situation on O’Connell, a Democrat, suggesting the mayor's approach to the issue is driven by ideology. However, Rich maintained that concerns among Broadway business owners cross political lines.
"This is not just a bunch of conservatives yelling about it," Rich said. "The group of business owners that I sat with were from both sides of the aisle."
"There's all kinds of things we don't agree on amongst each other," he continued. "But this right here brought unity amongst left and right and middle. It's that bad."
Rich also accused O’Connell of using tax policy to reshape the character of Nashville, offering his own view of the mayor's motivations.
Rich criticized Nashville Mayor Freddie O'Connell, suggesting that his approach to the issue is driven by ideology.  (Getty Images)

"It is a tactic to tax things out of existence that you don't like and replace them with things that you'd rather have there," Rich said. "Can you imagine the neon signs on Broadway replaced with government buildings and corporate offices? I think that's what he wants."
Fox News Digital has reached out to O’Connell’s office for comment.
The five-time Grammy Award nominee is now calling on Tennessee state leaders to intervene.

Rich said Broadway business owners have appealed to Tennessee House Speaker Cameron Sexton and Senate Majority Leader Jack Johnson and urged Gov. Bill Lee to work with lawmakers on a solution. He told Fox News Digital that the governor has the opportunity to become a "honky-tonk hero."
WATCH: JOHN RICH FEARS NASHVILLE’S NEON LIGHTS COULD GO DARK BEFORE SUPER BOWL COMES TO MUSIC CITY

"Governor Lee, who's still here, has an opportunity to do a special session with the Senate, with the House, and come with some solution that, if nothing else, will buy us some time until we can go in and make the more permanent moves," Rich said.

State leaders are considering taking action. Sexton's office confirmed to Axios Nashville on Wednesday that the House speaker has spoken with Lee's office about the issue and that they are "looking at all possible solutions," including the possibility of a special legislative session.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Despite his warnings, Rich said the culture that draws crowds to Broadway has not changed, at least not yet.
Rich said that Broadway's culture hasn't changed yet. (Johnny Louis/Getty Images)
"The culture on Broadway hasn't changed at all," he said. "The crowds that come there, the bands that play there, the owners of those businesses, they're the same as they've always been."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It is all about the music," Rich continued. "It's all about people coming to town to have a good time and look at what some of the most talented people you've ever seen in your life play on these tiny little stages."

title: Paris Jackson says dad Michael’s unusual rule helped protect her childhood
summary: Paris Jackson revealed on "Call Her Daddy" that Michael Jackson required his kids to finish homework and chores before enjoying Neverland attractions.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Behind the glitz of Michael Jackson’s larger-than-life world, Paris Jackson said her father enforced a strict rule to protect his children’s sense of normalcy.

The late King of Pop kept a tight rein on his children despite their unusual upbringing. Jackson recalled her father requiring them to finish their homework and chores before earning weekend fun, limiting television and movies and having them wear masks in public to shield their identities from the intense spotlight surrounding his fame.

"The cool, like very congruent line throughout my childhood that kind of started there and then just continued on wherever we went was, if you're good, and you do your chores, and you do your homework, and you do the things that you're supposed to do. Then on the weekends you can go see some animals, and you can go ride some rides, and you can go to the movies," she told "Call Her Daddy" host Alexandra Cooper.
VICTORIA BECKHAM REVEALS STRICT NO-PHONES RULE AT FAMILY DINNER KEEPS HER KIDS GROUNDED
Paris Jackson said her father, Michael Jackson, required homework and chores before his children could enjoy weekend outings. (Evan Agostini/Invision/AP, File)

"It was made very, very clear that all of the attractions [at Neverland] were not for us," she added. "That it did not belong to us. That was for, you know, underprivileged children and children that were terminally ill that couldn't go to like Disneyland."
Paris said the rule remained in place as the family moved frequently and rarely stayed anywhere for more than a year.

"If we were living in Vegas, and it's like, 'OK, if you're good you can go to Circus Circus on the weekends.' Or like we were in like some random place in Virginia. Like, 'OK, if you're good you can go to Chuck E. Cheese this weekend,'" she recalled.
Michael’s rules extended to television. Paris said his children could watch movies or TV after completing their responsibilities, with an exception of studying film without sound.
Paris Jackson recalled wearing masks in public as part of Michael Jackson’s effort to protect his children from the spotlight. (Dave M. Benett/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Michael also took steps to protect his children from the spotlight, having them wear masks in public so they could go unnoticed.

"I mean it just, it made sense because it was like, 'Oh yeah, if you do this now, then you can go to Chuck E. Cheese and be normal this weekend 'cause no one will know who you are,'" the "Wilted" singer recalled. "Like that made sense to me."
The masks helped Paris maintain some anonymity, but she still understood that her father was famous. What she didn’t grasp was the sheer magnitude of his celebrity.
Michael Jackson’s Neverland Ranch attractions were meant for visiting children, not his own family, Paris Jackson said. (Mohamed Hadid/Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I just didn't know how famous ... There was definitely part of me that, like when I looked out my hotel window, and it was one of the times where like the alias didn't work and there's just like a sea of people with signs and stuff – I'm not so naive to think, yeah, everyone experiences this, you know?" Paris admitted. "I just didn't understand the lengths."
Jackson, the only daughter of late pop superstar and Debbie Rowe, built an entertainment career through modeling, acting and music.

Paris Jackson has since built her own career in modeling, acting and music, releasing her debut album, "Wilted," in 2020. Her brothers, Prince and Bigi, have also built careers in the entertainment industry. (Alan Chapman/Getty Images)

After making highly publicized appearances with her family following Michael Jackson's 2009 death, she pursued modeling and landed acting roles before signing with Republic Records and releasing her debut album, Wilted, in 2020.

title: Jeffrey Dean Morgan nearly quit acting after miserable ‘Star Trek’ experience: ‘I hated it so much’
summary: Jeffrey Dean Morgan says his Xindi alien role on "Star Trek: Enterprise" nearly ended his career due to claustrophobia from 14-hour prosthetics sessions.
story: The "Doc Meets World" star spoke with Fox News Digital at Tribeca Festival about nearly leaving Hollywood and the lasting passion that kept drawing him back.
Jeffrey Dean Morgan's miserable experience playing an alien on "Star Trek: Enterprise" nearly convinced him to quit acting for good.

Long before his breakout roles on "Supernatural" and "Grey's Anatomy," Morgan appeared as a Xindi alien named Damron on the sci-fi series — a job that required extensive prosthetics and left the actor struggling with claustrophobia.
"I hated it so much," Morgan recalled during an appearance on Josh Horowitz's "Happy Sad Confused" podcast. "I was like, 'That's it. I've got to do something else.'"

title: Molly Sims calls out Hollywood for lying about beauty secrets
summary: Molly Sims slammed Hollywood's fake beauty secrets, saying stars lie about drinking water and sleep when facelifts and peptides tell the real story.
story: Model Molly Sims reveals her favorite wellness routines and why feeling good matters most at the Super Bowl.
Molly Sims is getting real about Hollywood spewing fake beauty secrets.

"Early on, other models would help you. Like, 'I’m getting shots in my a--,' or 'I’m only going to drink grapefruit juice,'" she explained. "Hollywood people would say, 'I just drink a lot of water, and I slept eight hours.' I’m like, 'No, you f---ing didn’t.'"

Sims slammed Hollywood for spewing fake beauty secrets. (Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for Baby2Baby)
MARTHA STEWART GETS CANDID ABOUT PLASTIC SURGERY, DATING AS SHE TURNS 85

The model also spoke about how her approach to her appearance has evolved from her early days in the modeling industry to now, as a woman in her 50s.

title: Nick Reiner indicted in murders of parents Rob Reiner, Michele Singer Reiner at Brentwood home
summary: Nick Reiner faces two murder charges and special circumstance allegations in the stabbing deaths of his parents at their Brentwood home in December.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty Wednesday after a grand jury indicted him on murder charges in the stabbing deaths of his parents, actor-director Rob Reiner and photographer-producer Michele Singer Reiner.

The indictment, returned July 20 and unsealed Wednesday, charged Nick, 32, with two counts of murder and included special circumstance allegations of multiple murders and lying in wait. Prosecutors also alleged he used a knife.
"This was a profound betrayal by someone who was loved and trusted by the very people he is accused of killing," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said.
ROB REINER'S FINAL ROLE DRAWS FIERCE CRITICISM 6 MONTHS AFTER LEGENDARY DIRECTOR'S TRAGIC DEATH
Nick Reiner during his arraignment in Los Angeles County Superior Court in Los Angeles. (Chris Torres/Pool)

"The indictment unsealed today also adds a special circumstance allegation that the defendant committed the murders by means of lying in wait. We hope that by having a grand jury return an indictment in this case it will bring us one step closer to a trial and achieving justice."
Prosecutors claimed Nick fatally stabbed his father, 78, and mother, 70, on Dec. 14, 2025, at their Brentwood home.
ROB REINER'S SON NICK FIGHTS FOR $1.5M TRUST FUND ACCESS TO BANKROLL HIGH-POWERED MURDER TRIAL DEFENSE
Multiple agencies worked to find and arrest Nick, who was apprehended near the University of Southern California at approximately 9:15 p.m., hours after his parents' bodies were discovered.
Nick Reiner appeared in court earlier this year during an arraignment with Deputy Public Defender Kimberly Greene. (Chris Torres-Pool)
The 32-year-old initially pleaded not guilty to the double murder charges in February, one month after his powerhouse attorney, Alan Jackson, stepped down from the case.
Jackson told reporters during a news conference he had "no choice" but to withdraw from the case, citing circumstances beyond his and Nick's control as to why he abruptly resigned from the case.
NICK REINER LOSING POWERHOUSE DEFENSE ATTORNEY MAY COME DOWN TO MONEY, EXPERTS SAY
"Circumstances beyond our control, but more importantly, circumstances beyond Nick's control have dictated that," Jackson said during a news conference outside the courthouse.
"Sadly, it's made it impossible for us to continue our representation of Nick. I'm legally and I'm ethically prohibited from explaining all the reasons why."
Jackson remained adamant that Nick was "not guilty" of murdering his parents.
Attorney Alan Jackson said he had "no choice" but to resign from Nick's counsel earlier this year. (Derek Shook for Fox News Digital)

"We've investigated this matter top to bottom, back to front," Jackson said. "What we've learned — and you can take this to the bank — is that pursuant to the laws of this state, pursuant to the law in California, Nick Reiner is not guilty of murder."
Jackson arrived at the Reiner home less than 24 hours after the couple's bodies were discovered. Soon after, he signed on to represent Nick.
Kimberly Greene, the deputy public defender assigned to the case, spoke briefly with Nick after Jackson resigned and said Nick "was understanding that there was going to be a change in counsel."

Nick is being held without bail and remains in custody at the Twin Towers Correctional Facility in downtown Los Angeles after formally being charged with two counts of first-degree murder in the stabbing deaths of his parents.

title: Brooks Nader ditches bikini top in front of dad and sparks fierce fan debate

story: Brooks Nader tells Fox News Digital about growing up with conservative parents who banned two-piece bikinis and reveals why her "Baywatch" swimsuit gets the family seal of approval.

Brooks Nader turned a sun-soaked Sardinian getaway into a full-on family spectacle when the model ditched her swimsuit top in front of her dad and relatives – leaving everyone with nowhere to look but straight at the drama.

title: ‘Grease’ star Stockard Channing says she’s ‘happy being a recluse’ after leaving America
summary: Stockard Channing revealed her reclusive London lifestyle, morning routine with her dog and why her longtime partner's death shifted everything.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Stockard Channing admitted she's "happy being a recluse" as she reflected on her quiet lifestyle after fleeing the states for the United Kingdom.
The "Grease" star began living in London "just before COVID," a move she envisioned after the 2014 death of her partner of 25 years, producer Daniel Gilham.
"I've lived alone since I lost Daniel and I'm happy being a recluse," Channing wrote in an essay for The Sunday Times. "I was married four times before Daniel, and they all represent epochs of me.
HEATHER LOCKLEAR SAYS SHE LIVES 'FAR AWAY' FROM HOLLYWOOD AND STAYS OUT OF THE SOCIAL SCENE
Stockard Channing is content away from Hollywood, she explained in a new essay. (Alan Chapman)

"I grew up in the sixties, reacting to that repressed notion of marriage and sexuality from the fifties kinda like Rizzo," she noted. "Children were thought about and, yeah, I think about them now because it'd be great to have someone taking care of me. But, hey, children can be just as selfish as everybody else out there."
Channing, 82, confessed that Gilham's death "was more devastating than I realized; it had a lag effect."
‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’
"The pattern of my life shifted, so I shifted my life from Maine," she wrote of the move, which also vaguely coincided with Trump's second presidential bid.

"When I started playing 'The West Wing's first lady, Abbey Bartlet, in 1999, we were about to move to the second Bush administration," she wrote. "The cast had a good look at that Washington world, and there seemed to be a level of honest, intelligent discourse that is missing from 2026.
Channing starred as Rizzo in the classic 1978 film "Grease." (Paramount Pictures)
"People look at 'The West Wing' and go, 'Wow, wasn't it great when politicians had an ounce of integrity?' Abbey didn't suffer fools, and she's the character most like me in real life."
Channing reflected on an interaction with director Aaron Sorkin, who said he "wrote Abbey as the person he saw in me."

"I was quite short with him the first time we met," she wrote. "He was saying all these nice things, and I said, 'Look, I don't have time for flattery.' I didn't mean to be rude it was just one of those days."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Her days of stardom are slightly different from now as the "Six Degrees of Separation" actress detailed her morning routine, which begins at 7 a.m. when her dog wakes her up.
"After he's had his breakfast and I've made a strong pot of coffee, my dog walker takes him out and I go back to bed," she wrote. "My ideal morning."
Olivia Newton John, left; Didi Conn, right; and Channing, center, were part of the "Pink Ladies."  (Getty Images)
John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John captured the hearts of America with "Grease." (CBS )
"My duvet is covered in ink spots because for many years I've been keeping a diary. I sit there with my fountain pen and my thoughts. What do I feel about this or that?
"I only leave the bed when I need to go to the bathroom. At my age life is guided by bodily functions."
By 10 a.m., Channing pursues a "bit of exercise," but admitted that her "favorite exercise days are when I play hooky."

"I know that exercising is the right thing to do but my brain tells me to go hide behind the bike sheds," she wrote. "Lunch is my first meal of the day and I can follow a recipe, but if my ramen doesn't work out I give it to the dog.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"If I'm leaving the apartment I comb my hair, but I don't have a wardrobe of designer outfits. Well, I do, but they're all from the Eighties and Nineties. Do I care how I look? Most actors do although part of your job is not being self-conscious.
Stockard Channing earned an Academy Award nomination in 1994 for her role in "Six Degrees of Separation." (Gregg DeGuire/WireImage)
"But I've never considered myself as beautiful. And I'm not a celebrity 'tart.' I'm just me, take it or leave it."
Channing's fan base is vast, and she recognized how different age groups remember her as different characters.

"For younger girls it's 'Practical Magic,' for grown-ups it's 'The West Wing,' and for real grown-ups it's 'Grease,'" she wrote. "Although the critics weren't kind about Grease, it made tons of money and it still gets streamed a lot.

"I guess films are like songs: they take you back to a particular time in your life. Maybe a more innocent time."

title: John Hinckley Jr gives his thoughts on Jodie Foster 45 years after shooting Ronald Reagan to impress her
summary: John Hinckley Jr. reveals that Jodie Foster could have been a target herself, saying "fate went the other way" toward former President Ronald Reagan.
story: Jodie Foster spoke to Fox News Digital about being honored at a hand and foot ceremony on Friday.
John Hinckley Jr., the man who shot former President Ronald Reagan in 1981 to impress Jodie Foster, said he wants nothing but good things for the actress.

"I just wish Jodie Foster well," he said. "I don’t really see her movies, but I wish her well, and I know she’s doing quite well. And that’s all I can say: I just, I wish Jodie well, and I hope she has a good life."

The 71-year-old explained on the "Mark Joseph Show" in an exclusive preview shared with Entertainment Weekly that when he shot Reagan 45 years ago in a delusional state, he believed he would spend the rest of his life with the "Silence of the Lambs" actress.
REAGAN SHOOTER CALLS LINK TO WASHINGTON HOTEL ‘SPOOKY’ AFTER ALLEGED TRUMP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT AT SAME SITE
John Hinckley Jr., at left in his 1981 mugshot, spoke about Jodie Foster in a new interview. (Bureau of Prisons/Getty Images; Jamie McCarthy/WireImage)
The full episode will air on Wednesday.

"I wanted to have like this union with Jodie Foster and live the rest of my life with her and all these things that, of course, were delusional, but I was believing those things at that time. So, the best outcome would have been to just have like this union with Jodie Foster," Hinckley told Joseph after the host asked what he believed at the time would be the best thing that could come out of the shooting.
John Hinckley Jr. said he wishes Jodie Foster well. (Getty Images)

He explained that he believed at the time that Foster would "join me wherever I was. You know, I didn’t know if I was going to be in jail or hospital or what, but after things settled down, I had this notion that she was going to join me wherever I was."

It came out shortly after Hinckley’s assassination attempt that left Reagan with a broken rib, punctured lung and internal bleeding, that Hinckley was obsessed with Foster after seeing her in "Taxi Driver" and thought the shooting would make her notice him.
JODIE FOSTER HAUNTED BY HORRIFIC DOG TRAGEDY, BELIEVES SHE GAVE UP WHAT SHE LOVES MOST FOR SUCCESS
John Hinckley Jr. stands for a portrait in Williamsburg, Va., in 2022. (AFP via Getty Images)
Hinckley was found not guilty by reason of insanity after shooting the former president outside the Washington Hilton two months after he was elected.
Former White House press secretary James Brady was shot in the head and suffered brain damage and partial paralysis, which led to his death in 2014. His death was ruled a homicide.
Two other men were also wounded in the shooting.
Hinckley was committed to a psychiatric hospital after the trial and released in 2016. By 2022, he was living in Virginia without any court restrictions.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
President Ronald Reagan waves to the crowd outside the Hilton Hotel in Washington, D.C., just before an assassination attempt on March 30, 1981. (Consolidated New Pictures/AFP via Getty Images)
Hinckley admitted to Joseph, however, that, in his delusional state, Foster could have been a target herself.
"She definitely could have been a target. It’s just fate went the other way," Hinckley said. "But, yeah, she could have been a target. But, as fate turned out, it was Reagan instead of her."

In a 2022 interview with CBS, Hinckley apologized for his actions.
Jodie Foster on the set of "Taxi Driver" with Robert De Niro and director Martin Scorsese. (Corbis via Getty Images)
"I shot four people, and I’m sorry to the Reagan family, the Brady family, the other families of the victims," he said at the time. "I’m sorry to Jodie Foster for bringing her into this."

title: 'Fire Country' star Diane Farr reveals where she now lives after leaving Los Angeles behind
summary: Diane Farr reveals she left Los Angeles after 30 years for rural Washington and plans to split time between Vancouver and Spain in her "third act."
story: After long, 14-hour workdays, Diane Farr told Fox News Digital that she makes her Sundays count—spending time with friends, paddleboarding, e-biking and soaking up life on the water in the Pacific Northwest.
"Fire Country" star Diane Farr has revealed where she is now living after leaving Los Angeles behind.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, Farr explained that once her children went off to college, she didn't feel tied to California anymore and decided to put down roots in rural Washington. She also plans to split her time between Vancouver and Spain.

"So I actually moved to rural Washington because I could buy this pretty house, and it wasn't very expensive in comparison to living in LA for all those years," she said. "I live right on the water, so there's a lot of stand-up paddling and there's a lot of e-biking and really drinking in this gorgeous Pacific Northwest weather."
"Fire Country" star Diane Farr shared that she left LA for rural Washington after living in California for 30 years. (Sergei Bachlakov/CBS via Getty Images)
Farr stars in "Fire Country," which is filmed in Vancouver. Farr plays Sharon Leone on "Fire Country," a Cal Fire Division Chief and the mother of Bode Leone.
"Fire Country" Season 5 is scheduled to premiere on October 9, 2026, airing Fridays at 9/8c on CBS and streaming the next day on Paramount+.
Farr told Fox News Digital that once her children went off to college and left California, she felt like she had "permission" to do the same.
'FIRE COUNTRY' STAR DIANE FARR LEAVES LOS ANGELES AFTER 30 YEARS TO START HER 'THIRD ACT'
"So I actually moved to rural Washington because I could buy this pretty house, and it wasn't very expensive in comparison to living in LA for all those years."

"The permission came from my children being old enough that they live somewhere else. You know, they go to college, they live in other states, and I know women always talk about empty nest syndrome, and mine was unique," Farr began. "I didn't leave LA for 15 years when I had babies. I was afraid of working out of town. I was afraid of missing everything. I was afraid to do a one-hour drama."
WATCH: Diane Farr finds her joy in the Pacific Northwest
The actress explained that she had her children when she was nearly 40 and "really wanted to be there."

"After the pandemic, 15 years had gone by. We spent two years at home and everybody was a teenager and mean to mom. And I thought, I can leave, I could go to Vancouver. I'm taking that drama," she continued.
Shawn Hatosy as Brett Richards and Diane Farr as Sharon Leone in "Fire Country." (CBS via Getty Images)
Farr said that her "third act" was focused around how she could get more joy out of her life.
"My third act is gonna look like six months of the year in Spain and six months of the year in Vancouver, because it's really like how to get the joie de vie. It's how to live the most," Farr said.
WATCH: 'Fire Country' star Diane Farr teases Sharon’s 'off the rails' era in Season 5
At the end of July, Farr shared with her Instagram followers that she was leaving Los Angeles after 30 years.

"I wasn’t born here, I didn’t go to school here — I just had a chance for representation as an actor and I moved out of NYC the summer I was 26," she wrote. "I came like most of the people I love in Hollywoodland — none of which I saw this week bc moving sucks."
'VAMPIRE DIARIES' STAR IAN SOMERHALDER SAYS LEAVING HOLLYWOOD FOR FARMING 'SHIFTED MY LIFE FOREVER'
She went on to say that she came to Los Angeles "chasing a dream that I am still shocked worked out."
Michael Trucco as Luke Leone and Diane Farr as Sharon Leone in "Fire Country." (CBS via Getty Images)

Farr's acting career began in the '90s, with the actress landing her breakthrough role in "Roswell" in 1999. She later earned leading roles in "Numb3rs," "Splitting Up Together" and, most recently, "Fire Country."
In addition to her acting career, Farr also reflected on the many other positive experiences she had while living in Los Angeles, including starting a family.

"I also got to raise babies in the sun and the mountains and enjoy this beautiful home and attend public schools ??" she said. "Pinch me I’m overwhelmed by the blessings and hope, really hope I gave enough back. LA will always be where my family is from."
WATCH: 'Fire Country' star Diane Farr is choosing joy in her 'third act'
Farr shares three children with her ex-husband, Seung Yong Chung: son Beckett, 18, and twin daughters Coco and Sawyer, 17.

Speaking to Fox News Digital, Farr explained what fans can expect from Sharon in season five.

"Well, last year was a lot of grief, right? Because she had lost Vince and this year she seems to have gotten some action with a very handsome man at the end of last season. So, I was sort of looking at it like Sharon hasn't dated or been single or been a party of one since she's about 20," she began. "So she's a little off the rails, you know, like she's kind of behaving like a 20-year-old. Which isn't good when you're the boss, and you have children and people responsible for you."
Farr shares twin teenage daughters and a son with her ex-husband. (Francis Specker/CBS via Getty Images)
Farr concluded, "So, she's not making her best choices this season."

title: Meghan Markle’s royal exit had warning signs years earlier, veteran correspondent reveals
summary: Simon Vigar's new book details how Meghan Markle's 2018 royal tour of Australia exposed the first cracks in her relationship with palace staff.
story: Simon Vigar, author of "The Four Wives of Windsor," says a "culture clash" and mismatched expectations contributed to Meghan Markle’s difficulties adjusting to life in the British royal family.
Meghan Markle’s rocky tenure as a working royal may have stemmed from a "culture clash" with palace aides, according to a veteran royal correspondent who covered her time as a working royal.
Simon Vigar, one of Britain's longest-serving royal correspondents, examines those tensions in his new book, "The Four Wives of Windsor."
Kensington Palace told Fox News Digital it does not comment on books. A spokesperson for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex told Fox News Digital, "This is not something we would comment on."
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S HOLLYWOOD DREAMS HIT WALL AS EXPERT WARNS OF ‘TOXIC BRAND’ STIGMA

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex visit a local farming family, the Woodleys, on Oct. 17, 2018 in Dubbo, Australia. Simon Vigar looked back on the couple's royal tour in his new book, "The Royal Wives of Windsor." (Chris Jackson - Pool/Getty Images)

"There was a culture clash there," Vigar told Fox News Digital. "I think it's a crying shame. It was avoidable, and egos got in the way on both sides. I think she thought that there would be more control over events, public events, than there was. ... The narrative now is that the British media was always against Harry and Meghan. That is not how I remember it, and many of my colleagues remember it."

"Harry and Meghan were great," Vigar said. "I saw her on her first engagement in Nottingham. She was brilliant with the crowds. She was an absolute natural, which is why it's so sad that they're not part of [the working royals] now. The tour of Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and Tonga [in 2018] went really well.
Meghan Markle visits Nottingham for her first official public engagement with then-fiancé Prince Harry on Dec. 1, 2017, in Nottingham, England. (Jeremy Selwyn - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"The crowds were massive. But ... the palace press officers were trying to spin three different stories after that. One person was in tears from the Kensington Palace team because of how it had all gone pear-shaped, as we say in the U.K."
WATCH: MEGHAN MARKLE FACED ROYAL FAMILY ‘CULTURE CLASH’: AUTHOR

Meghan, a former American actress who starred in the legal drama "Suits," became the Duchess of Sussex when she married Prince Harry in 2018. The palace announced Meghan's pregnancy shortly after the couple arrived in Sydney for their royal tour that October.

Vigar covered the royal tour and wrote that it exposed some of the first significant cracks in Meghan's role as a working royal. According to Vigar, Meghan was accustomed to a public life where "everything was micromanaged in a far more controlled environment."
Meghan Markle on the red carpet for "Suits," circa 2015. (Mike Coppola/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

"Those levels of Hollywood control-freakery, as courtiers say, are incompatible with the public service role of the monarchy," he wrote. Vigar also quoted an anonymous senior staffer as saying, "My overall sense is Meghan realized it was hard work and not that glamorous. It's not about you."
Simon Vigar's "The Four Wives of Windsor" is available now. Vigar is one of British television's longest-serving royal correspondents. (Penguin)

Vigar wrote that during the royal tour, Meghan was scheduled to visit Suva Market in Fiji for an engagement highlighting women's economic empowerment. She planned to meet with vendors connected to the cause, but the visit ended earlier than planned.

"There were all these people queuing up to meet her," Vigar recalled. "... In the first few minutes, it all ended very quickly. Team Sussex said it was a security issue. That is denied by other people."

Meghan Markle’s first pregnancy was officially announced on Oct. 15, 2018, when Kensington Palace confirmed that she and Prince Harry were expecting their first child, due in spring 2019. She was reported to be around 12 weeks pregnant at the time. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Reports at the time attributed the shortened visit to security concerns as crowds gathered to see Meghan.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, visits Suva Market to meet female vendors involved in the U.N. Women's project "Markets for Change" on Oct. 24, 2018, in Suva, Fiji. (Pool/Getty Images)

"... If it was a security issue, the Scotland Yard bodyguards would never have allowed her to arrive. They have an advanced team there. They have a team with her. They wouldn't have let her get out of the car if they thought it was a big security issue."

"Was it because it was too chaotic or too hot? Well, it wasn't chaotic really," Vigar said. "It was a very well-planned route through the market. It may have been illness, although that's not what Team Sussex said. In which case, why come down in the first place? And she looked OK. [But] there was a moment in the market where she looked at one of her assistants and the whole mood changed. It all went fast-forward. And my cameraman was being pushed out of the way."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend the unveiling of The Queen's Commonwealth Canopy in Redvale, New Zealand, on Oct. 30, 2018. (New Zealand Herald - Pool/Getty Images)

"The women I was with had been waiting for ages to see her," Vigar continued. "One of them had handmade raffia fans with Harry and Meghan in them. She didn't get to meet her. She just zoomed past her, and that was that. Meghan was off. It was very strange. ... And I suppose that was an early sign in retrospect. That was an early sign that there was a mismatch in expectations."
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex attends the official opening of the ANZAC Memorial at Hyde Park in Sydney, Australia, on Oct. 20, 2018. (Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)
Vigar noted that the Duchess of Sussex was working on "an intense schedule" while pregnant during the overseas tour.
"Meghan understood ‘the show’ bit but not the cultural side of the royal family," one senior aide told Vigar.
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex attends the Jaguar Land Rover Driving Challenge at the Invictus Games on Oct. 20, 2018, in Sydney. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

Valentine Low, then royal correspondent for The Times of London, reported in 2021 that Jason Knauf, who had served as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex’s communications secretary, had submitted a bullying complaint concerning Meghan in 2018. The Sussexes’ lawyers rebutted the allegations, while a spokesperson for the couple said the duchess was "saddened by this latest attack on her character."

Meghan Markle is seen here being interviewed by Oprah Winfrey on March 8, 2021. The bombshell report concerning bullying allegations was published shortly before the televised tell-all. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

Vigar argued that Meghan didn't just marry a prince. She also entered an institution with its own rules, rhythms and intense press scrutiny — a sharp contrast with Hollywood, where, he said, publicists can exert far more control over appearances, interviews and publicity.

"The press team at Kensington Palace is pretty small, let's say, compared to a movie premiere in Hollywood or a movie premiere in London," he explained. "It's a tiny press team, and they're involved in this institution, this royal family, which is on the front pages almost every single day. They have to roll with it. They have to roll with events, and they have to try and shape them in the best way they can."
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex walk along Kingfisher Bay Jetty on Oct. 22, 2018, in Fraser Island, Australia. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"Harry understood it," Vigar argued. "Meghan, by her own admission, didn't know much about the British royal family or who some of them were. It was just a different level of expectation. Whereas Catherine, Camilla, Lady Diana Spencer, who was an aristocrat and the most aristocratic of all four of them, they just understood the British family even more. I think the problem was it was a culture clash. It's an American lady marrying into the most upper-class British family possible."
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend the Invictus Games Opening Ceremony on Oct. 20, 2018, in Sydney. (Samir Hussein / WireImage)
A royal aide told Vigar that working royals are expected to fulfill public engagements even when they do not feel their best: "Even if they are feeling grotty, they turn up and they do the job."
In the book, Vigar wrote that there is nothing "showbiz" about "cold palaces and a life of smiling, waving and turning up."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex are seen greeting members of the public at the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia on April 17, 2026, in Sydney, Australia. According to reports, several palace employees left their positions while working for Harry and Meghan. "That's obviously what Harry and Meghan believe, but I know, and my colleagues know that actually, the reverse is true. People were working very hard to support her. And unfortunately, it didn't work out, and it went downhill … By the end of 2019, they both wanted out."

title: ‘Twilight’ star Kellan Lutz traded California for Tennessee land and Bible studies
summary: Kellan Lutz explains how his wife's need for a support system after their second child led the family from Orange County to Franklin, Tennessee.
story: Dennis Quaid reflects on leaving Los Angeles for Nashville, saying residents are frustrated with high taxes, poor services and the fallout from devastating wildfires.
Kellan Lutz said this week that he left California three years ago for Tennessee after the pandemic.
"I love California, I really do," he explained on "Inside of You" with Michael Rosenbaum. "The whole Tennessee move happened when we had our second kid."
The "Twilight" actor said they moved from Orange County – and his wife, Brittany Lutz, hopes to eventually move back there or at least to be "bi-ish coastal."
‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’
Kellan Lutz said that his family moved to Tennessee three years ago. (WireImage)

Lutz’s wife was born and raised in Orange County. "Her family is awesome. But post-COVID, a lot of people flew, like fled California. A lot of people lost jobs and wanted to move somewhere a little bit more peace given."

His wife’s family chose to leave California, and he said they followed them to Tennessee, mainly because otherwise she wouldn’t have had a support system when he goes on location for work, and she’s left at home with the children.
"We got some land, got great Bible studies that we're a part of, great churches, great community,"

"And one of the kids got sick. She felt really out of control as far as not being able to bring both kids there or just kind of helpless. So, she's like, ‘Can we move?’ I'm like, ‘Yeah, of course," he explained.
He added that other men with kids in his life told him that new moms usually wanted to move to where their mom lives "just to help with the kids."
Kellan Lutz is seen at an event with wife, Brittany, in 2019. (WireImage)
'VAMPIRE DIARIES' STAR IAN SOMERHALDER SAYS LEAVING HOLLYWOOD FOR FARMING 'SHIFTED MY LIFE FOREVER'

"Then when they decided to move, I was like, "OK, well, we're going to do it. We're going to give it a couple years and we have, and it's great. There's a lot of great things about Tennessee, especially Franklin where we live."
The family moved to Tennessee three years ago, but he acknowledged he doesn’t know how long they’ll stay.
Kellan Lutz signing autographs for "Twilight" fans in 2009. (WireImage)

"We got some land, got great Bible studies that we're a part of, great churches, great community," he said. "There's a lot of actors. I've gone to probably more movie premieres in Franklin, Tennessee, than I have in L.A., you know, the last couple years since I lived there."
Admittedly though, there are adjustments.

"Like we aren't seasons people," he said. "There's tornadoes. My wife goes on red alert, especially when you have kids. And we do miss good sushi and good Mexican food."

title: ‘The Office’ star Lucy Davis ‘at peace’ with 'incurable' cancer diagnosis after nearly ignoring warning sign
summary: Lucy Davis revealed her breast cancer has metastasized to her spine, hip and ribs, with chemotherapy no longer an option for "The Office" actress.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Lucy Davis revealed a devastating Stage 4 breast cancer diagnosis after quietly battling the disease for the past year and a half.
"The Office" actress said the cancer had metastasized to her spine, right hip and ribs and was now "incurable," with chemotherapy no longer an option.

"The initial lump that I felt, wasn’t a ‘lump’ as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny," she wrote on Instagram. "I almost didn’t bother getting it checked. So I guess I’m saying don’t ignore anything – get everything checked out."
Rather than dwell on her prognosis, Davis said she was determined to embrace whatever time she had left.
BARRY MANILOW RESCHEDULES CONCERT 45 MINUTES BEFORE START AMID ONGOING LUNG CANCER RECOVERY
‘The Office’ actress Lucy Davis is opening up about her private battle with incurable Stage 4 breast cancer – and the subtle symptom she almost ignored. (Frederick M. Brown/Getty Images)

"As of now, I’m trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can," she explained. "I always like to find the teachable moments in anything negative that happens. And cancer has not disappointed in that regard; there’s a lot I have learned from it, and I’m grateful for that."
Davis said maintaining that outlook had not made the physical realities of cancer any easier.

"As some of you will know, the pain can really be something else," Davis wrote. "Standing and walking for too long a time can be hard, and I need to use a wheelchair sometimes (so if you see me toddling around in one, feel free to give me a push!)"
Despite the pain, Davis said she had found peace with what could come next.
"The Office" star Lucy Davis says she’s choosing joy, purpose and peace as she continues acting and advocating for animal rights amid her cancer diagnosis. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I’m not scared of whatever comes next," she said. "I’m at peace with it. I’ll see my Gracie sooner than expected, and for me, leaving my physical body just means going home. Any and all grieving is for my family; it’s far harder for them than for me."
But Davis made clear she had no plans to stop pursuing the work and causes she loved.

"I’m still going to keep up all my work for animal rights," Davis noted. "It’s so important to me. And I still would like to keep working. I’m perfectly able to do so, and acting is one of the biggest joys in my life."
After an 18-month battle kept largely out of the public eye, Lucy Davis shared an emotional update on cancer’s physical toll and the outlook keeping her going. (Dave Benett/Getty Images)

Simon Pegg, Lucy Davies and Nick Frost attend the U.K. premiere of "Shaun of the Dead" on March 30, 2004. (Dave Benett/Getty Images)

Davis began acting in the 1990s, with an early role as Maria Lucas in the BBC’s acclaimed 1995 adaptation of "Pride and Prejudice." Her major breakthrough came as receptionist Dawn Tinsley in Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant’s original British version of "The Office," which ran from 2001 to 2003 and became an international comedy phenomenon.

title: Riley Green shares how Luke Grimes unexpectedly launched his acting career
summary: Riley Green reveals how Luke Grimes encouraged him to audition for "Marshals," helping the country star land his first acting role as a Navy SEAL.
story: Riley Green told Fox News Digital that he doesn't get nervous going on stage anymore, but his nerves were wrecked when he walked on the "Marshals" set.
Riley Green may be one of country music’s rising stars, but his latest on-screen career move came with a little help from a famous friend.

During an appearance on "CBS Mornings" on Monday, the 37-year-old Alabama native revealed that "Yellowstone" star Luke Grimes helped open the door to his first acting role, encouraging Green to step outside his comfort zone and eventually helping land him a part on the CBS drama "Marshals."

"It happened so organically because he was starting his music career and coming to Nashville a little bit. We wrote together," said Green, who made his acting debut as Garrett — a former Navy SEAL struggling with PTSD — alongside Grimes in the "Yellowstone" spinoff.
TAYLOR SHERIDAN SHOCKS 'YELLOWSTONE' FANS WITH NEW SPINOFF SERIES, PROVIDES VIEWERS WITH DARK RIDE
Riley Green opened up about how his friendship with Luke Grimes led to an unexpected career move. (Getty Images)

"He mentioned something about maybe I should act. I said, 'Well I'm interested.' He said, 'I've got this show.' A couple months later, I went out and read for a part. They said I got it. I flew back out to Utah and we filmed the show."
Earlier this year, Green admitted it's not every day an opportunity like that presents itself.

"I guess that doesn't happen all the time, where the star of the show sits in with somebody trying out for a part," Green told USA Today. "But man, I've got to be such good friends with Luke, and it makes it so much easier to step into a world that I wasn't necessarily comfortable in."
It was a dramatic change for a performer accustomed to playing sold-out concerts.
TAYLOR SHERIDAN’S 'YELLOWSTONE’ FORMULA TURNS COUNTRY STARS INTO SCENE-STEALERS AS MORGAN WADE MAKES HER DEBUT
Green previously admitted acting was considerably more intimidating than taking the stage.
Riley Green as Garrett and Luke Grimes as Kayce Dutton appear in a scene from the CBS original series "Marshals." (Cam McLeod/CBS)

"I don’t get nervous going on stage anymore," Green previously told Fox News Digital at the "Marshals" premiere. "I’ve played enough shows now it kind of comes naturally, but this was a completely different world, and it’s not my set, it’s not my stage."
His Hollywood debut was the latest unexpected chapter in a career Green never necessarily envisioned for himself.
Long before he found fame, Green was earning his living as a construction worker, framing homes until he signed a record deal in 2018.
LAINEY WILSON SAYS CITY PEOPLE HAVE WRONG VIEW OF COUNTRY TOWNS AS SHE DEFENDS HER 'BLUE COLLAR' ROOTS
And according to Green, he wouldn't have been able to handle the spotlight at the time.

"I've been so fortunate that my success was gradual," he told the CBS hosts. "Early 20s, I don't know if I could have handled what I've got going on right now, but it's been really motivating. I've done it for well over 10 years now."
Green prefers life on his farm over Hollywood fame.  (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)

"I was building houses for a living. And I signed a record deal in 2018 and put my tool belt up and really went on the road heavy and it's just, as a songwriter, it's so great when people are like relating to the music, and you hear them singing those songs back to you."

"When you see it growing, it just makes you want to go play more shows and keep grinding," he continued. "So it's a really great time to be in country music because I think the genre as a whole is becoming more popular everywhere."

Green signed with Big Machine Label Group in 2018 and broke through with "There Was This Girl," followed by hits including "I Wish Grandpas Never Died," "Half of Me," "Different 'Round Here," "You Look Like You Love Me" with Ella Langley and "Worst Way."
Yet despite his success — and his unexpected entry into Hollywood — Green has remained closely tied to the life he had before fame.
Prior to finding mega success as a country music star, Green made a living as a construction worker framing homes.  (Christopher Polk/Dick Clark Productions via Getty Images)

He continues to live on his farm in Alabama rather than relocating full-time to Nashville.

title: Bella Thorne says Hollywood treated her like a kid on screen and an adult off camera
summary: Bella Thorne opens up about the moment she turned 18 and finally felt free after years of navigating Hollywood's impossible child star expectations.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Bella Thorne's life as a child star came with a harsh reality: Hollywood expected her to be a kid on screen and an adult everywhere else.

Thorne began working in entertainment as a child, appearing as a model before taking on television roles in shows including HBO’s "Big Love." Her major breakthrough arrived in 2010 when she was cast as CeCe Jones opposite Zendaya’s Rocky Blue in Disney Channel’s "Shake It Up."
"You're ... spending all of your hours a day on set with adults, you know, that is – it's like such a different, the brain's like how do I–" Thorne explained during an appearance on "Call Her Daddy."
GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'
Bella Thorne reflected on the pressures of growing up in Hollywood during a recent appearance on Alexandra Cooper’s podcast. (Getty Images)

"And I'm expected to be this child, but I'm also working like hours like an adult and being in adult conversations," she added. "And when I f--k up it's my bad, not like a child – It's my bad. Like you're an adult, it's your bad."
But navigating those adult expectations while growing up in the public eye didn't come easily for Thorne.

"Well, I think people can see how I've managed it publicly," she told host Alexandra Cooper. "They can see it, they've got photos of it. Oh, they got all the photos. Oh, wow. I don't know that I ever handled it or balanced it out correctly."

"I don't think that I ever had that mental clarity," Thorne acknowledged. "I've worked a lot on the more recent side. I got to a point where I just needed to kind of change things in my life and get better at – I was working so much and yet was leaving very little time for the things that I really, really cared about."
Bella Thorne rose to Disney Channel fame alongside Zendaya after starring in "Shake It Up" as CeCe Jones. (Craig Sjodin/Disney Channel via Getty Images)
FORMER DISNEY STAR MAITLAND WARD SAYS YOUNG ACTORS WERE TREATED LIKE A 'PRODUCT' IN HOLLYWOOD FACTORY

Thorne said she spent the past two years working to prioritize her mental health, a shift that became especially important after "Color Your Hurt" left her feeling emotionally drained. The now 28-year-old actress revealed she finally gave herself "some space to breathe" along with grace.
"I don't think I ever did that when I was younger," she said.
While Thorne struggled to give herself that same grace as a child star, she recalled feeling a dramatic shift when she turned 18.
Bella Thorne said she felt a sense of freedom when she turned 18 after years of working as a child actor. (Vittorio Zunino Celotto/Getty Images)
"...I was like, 'I'm free,'" the "Midnight Sun" star recalled.

"Like I'm literally free. Like I'm walking into this house and no one's asking me when I'm like, when I'm gonna be there, when this time or when I'm gonna leave. It ... was such a weird – and you don't know what's weird until someone else tells you it's weird."
Thorne also spoke candidly about being compared to her fellow Disney Channel stars, including Selena Gomez, Miley Cyrus and Demi Lovato.

Bella Thorne said comparisons to fellow Disney stars including Miley Cyrus, Selena Gomez and Demi Lovato began when she was just 12. Pictured with Zendaya. (Craig Sjodin/Disney Channel via Getty Images)

"I didn't so much hang out with people from the network," Thorne recalled. "I hung out with Zendaya, we hung out ... 'Shake It Up' was in a different time when Miley and Selena and Demi and those shows – They were all, I think 16, 17 when we were starting. So the eras are so different, and yet they intersect."
She said people questioned whether she would become Disney's next "bad girl," something she struggled to comprehend at such a young age.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Bella Thorne opened up about the mental-health work she has prioritized over the past two years. (Gary Miller/Getty Images for Glass House Brands)

"And I remember when I was 12, people asking me if I was gonna be – comparing us all, all the Disney girls and with Miley and Selena and this new era – and asking which was gonna be the next bad girl," Thorne claimed. "And, 'Are you gonna be like Lindsay Lohan?' And like all these things at 12, 13 – you're just, your brain is like trying so hard. 'Like am I gonna be like what? Like what? What is the question?' Like, oh my God."
Thorne later moved beyond her Disney image with a steady mix of film and television roles.
Thorne has also made a bigger push behind the camera. In August 2026, she signed on to write, direct and star in "Spring Breakers 2," following her feature directorial debut, "Color Your Hurt."

title: Kaia Gerber owns 'nepo baby' status while questioning other celebrity kids: 'Show me why you deserve this job'
summary: Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere tackle the nepo baby debate in Vogue's September cover story as they star together in Ryan Murphy's FX series "The Shards."
story: The "Desperate Housewives" star shared how he thinks his children benefited from growing up outside Los Angeles.
Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere are confronting Hollywood’s "nepo baby" debate head-on.

In Vogue’s September 2026 cover story, Gerber, daughter of supermodel Cindy Crawford, and Gere, son of Hollywood star Richard Gere opened up about the scrutiny surrounding their careers as they step into the spotlight together in Ryan Murphy’s FX series "The Shards" and acknowledged that audiences may be quick to judge them because of their famous families.
GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'
Kaia Gerber, the daughter of supermodel Cindy Crawford, fully owns her "nepo baby" status. (FilmMagic)
"I’ve only ever been a nepo baby, and I’ve only ever benefited in my career from it," Gerber, 24, told Vogue.
The model and actress admitted she can even be skeptical of other celebrity children herself, wondering whether they have earned the opportunities they receive.
"Okay, show me why you deserve this job."
Gerber said she warned her 26-year-old co-star that audiences likely wouldn't view him the same way they would an unknown actor making his debut.
CHARLIZE THERON SAYS HER KIDS WON’T GET A FREE RIDE IN HOLLYWOOD: THEY NEED TO ‘EARN IT’

"Unfortunately with this show, it’s not like you’re just any unknown actor and people will judge you as an unknown actor," she recalled telling him, adding that the scrutiny has made her "want to work harder."
Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere discuss "nepo baby" labels in Vogue's September issue.  (VOGUE; Steven Meisel)
Gerber began modeling as a child and has since branched into acting, including multiple projects with Murphy.
Gere took a different route into show business.
Despite growing up with an A-list father, he said he was raised largely outside Hollywood and had never stepped onto a professional set until last year.
SHARON STONE SAYS 'EUPHORIA' SHOULD BE SHOWN IN 'EVERY HIGH SCHOOL' AND REQUIRED VIEWING FOR PARENTS
Initially, Gere brushed off suggestions that he might follow in his parents’ footsteps and studied visual arts at Brown University before becoming involved in student filmmaking.
It wasn't until a talent manager saw one of his student films, that his acting career really began. He later auditioned for both "The Shards" and HBO’s "Euphoria," landing roles in each.
Gerber is very aware of her privileged upbringing and says it only benefited her career.  (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
Gere acknowledged that his family name inevitably complicates perceptions of his success.

"I’m a very self-critical guy who would like to believe that my career’s going well for all the wrong reasons," he told Vogue, adding that continued success has made that increasingly difficult for him to believe.
MAYA HAWKE SAYS MOM UMA THURMAN PRACTICED 'WITCH-ADJACENT' REMEDIES
The casting of Gerber and Gere carries an additional Hollywood twist.
Cindy Crawford was 22 when she started dating 39-year-old actor Richard Gere.` (Brenda Chase/Online USA, Inc./Getty Images)

Crawford and Richard Gere were married from 1991 to 1995 and famously appeared together on the cover of Vogue in 1992. More than three decades later, their children now share the magazine’s September cover while starring opposite each other in "The Shards."
For Gerber, however, escaping comparisons to her famous mother — and assumptions about how she landed her career — may prove impossible.

Rather than run from the "nepo baby" conversation, she appears determined to let the work make her case.

title: 'Blue Bloods' star Jennifer Esposito says she was locked in psych ward as health battle spiraled
summary: Jennifer Esposito reveals how celiac disease caused liver failure, a psychiatric ward stay and thoughts of suicide before doctors finally diagnosed her.
story: Donnie Wahlberg told Fox News Digital that he did everything he could to keep "Blue Bloods" on-air before pivoting to the spin-off series.
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Jennifer Esposito is opening up about the yearslong health battle that she says derailed her career, left her severely depressed and eventually landed her in a psychiatric ward before doctors diagnosed her with celiac disease.

During an appearance on Maria Menounos' "Heal Squad" podcast, Esposito, 53, recalled being a young actress in New York City when unexplained physical and mental health problems became so debilitating that she was forced to put her life on hold.
"I had a whole life beginning in the city, and I was a young actor and I had to stop everything," Esposito said.
MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS
Jennifer Esposito detailed years of misdiagnoses before she was ultimately diagnosed with celiac disease. (WireImage)
The actress said she became "deeply depressed" and began having "thoughts of suicide" as doctors struggled to determine what was wrong.

"They brought me to a psychologist, like they had me on every medication," she recalled. "They wanted to give me shock treatment at one point because I wasn't responding. I'm very sensitive to medication. It was a really bad time. And my mother had people pray over me."
Esposito said she eventually began to suspect that her physical and mental health symptoms could be connected to nutrition.
"I realized that there was a major connection with what I was eating and my vitamins and then my body," she said.
DAMON WAYANS REVEALS THE SCARY SYMPTOM THAT LED TO HIS TYPE 2 DIABETES DIAGNOSIS
Her health began to "collapse" while she was working on the ABC comedy "Samantha Who?," which aired from 2007 to 2009, according to the actress.
Esposito recalled experiencing alarming physical symptoms, including losing her hair and fingernails.
The 53-year-old actress said the symptoms took a toll on her physically and mentally. (JC Olivera/Getty Images)
"I had hair falling out, nails falling off," she said.
Then, she said, a tooth fell out while she was filming a scene.
CARLY SIMON REVEALS THE COMMON CONDITION THAT MASKED HER PARKINSON'S DIAGNOSIS
"A tooth fell out of my mouth, like literally in the middle of a scene," Esposito recalled. "I was mortified but also had been so ill that I just — I went hysterical. Like, somebody has to help me."

Esposito said she was misdiagnosed several times, with doctors considering conditions including multiple sclerosis and irritable bowel syndrome. She said a therapist suggested stress was behind her symptoms.
"Talk about gaslighting," she said.

"We don't ever treat the actual underlying issue. We treat symptoms in this country, in America," Esposito continued. "I went for years on that, and I tried everything myself. I went to holistic healers. I went to get my aura cleansed. I was vegan."
Desperate for answers, Esposito said she began attending a non-denominational church in an effort to "feel recharged."
On one drive there, she recalled reaching a breaking point.
Esposito said she was losing her hair and nails were falling off due to her nutrition issues. (Getty Images)

"I remember saying to myself, because I was so depressed of being so sick all the time and fighting panic disorders … ‘If you don't get a diagnosis, you have to accept the fact that you're crazy, and you've created this, and you're going to let it go because I can't keep doing this.’"
Moments later, she said, a large piece of wood flew from a truck in front of her and smashed through her windshield.
RANDY TRAVIS' HEALTH CRISIS BEGAN WITH 'CONGESTION' AND ENDED IN A FIVE-MONTH HOSPITAL STAY
"I'm sitting with glass all over me," Esposito said. After managing to pull to the side of the road, she took the frightening accident as a sign to continue looking for answers.
Two days later, Esposito said, a doctor called with her diagnosis: celiac disease.
"I’m not sure how you’re alive," Esposito recalled the doctor telling her.
According to Esposito, her case was so severe that her liver was failing.
The "Blue Bloods" star recalls being taken to a psych ward amid her misdiagnoses period. (Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition in which consuming gluten — a protein found in wheat, barley and rye — triggers an immune response that damages the small intestine. That damage can interfere with the body's ability to absorb nutrients and can cause symptoms extending well beyond the digestive system, including fatigue, anemia, neurological problems and elevated liver enzymes. A strict, lifelong gluten-free diet is the primary treatment and can allow the intestine to heal, according to the Mayo Clinic.
After receiving her diagnosis, Esposito immediately eliminated gluten from her diet, but said her body was in such poor condition that her recovery was grueling.

She recalled being severely deficient in vitamin D and developing welts when exposed to sunlight. Her nervous system was also so overwhelmed, she said, that ordinary stimulation became difficult to tolerate.

"They had me on four Klonopin a day, and I was still a trembling mess," Esposito said. "I was literally sleeping in my kitchen because it was the only place that didn't have a window, because the light — the stimulus from the light — would make me tremble and shake."
'GAME OF THRONES' ACTRESS SAYS SHE JOINED A WELLNESS CULT THAT LED TO A PSYCHOTIC BREAK
"It was horrendous," she added.
About two months after her diagnosis, Esposito began seeing a medical expert who she said wanted to study her because of the severity of her case.
Esposito said she eventually took matters into her own hands. (Getty Images)
She underwent regular blood and urine testing, but during one appointment, Esposito said she was in such distress that she pleaded with the doctor to keep her in the hospital.
"Doctor, you got to keep me here because I'm jumping out of my skin. I'm going to jump out the window," she recalled saying.
Esposito said the remark was interpreted as a threat of self-harm.
Within half an hour, she said, she was taken to a psychiatric ward under the alias "Betty Franklin."
"I will say it was seven of the most excruciating hours of my entire life because I was yet again pleading for my sanity," she said.
Esposito said her father was with her and recalled fearing that she would not get out if he left.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"If you leave me here, I'm dying because I'm going to fight these people," she recalled thinking.
The actress said the experience became even more frightening when a doctor asked her father for permission to restrain her if she got "out of hand."
Esposito hopes her story can help others.  (FilmMagic)
Esposito forced herself to remain calm. "I thought, if I ever get out of here, I have to do something," she said.
After returning home, Esposito said she took an increasingly active role in understanding her condition and recovery.
"If you heal your gut, I promise you, not everything can go away," she said, adding that recovery "takes time."
Esposito, who said she now lives outside the United States, told Menounos that she no longer experiences panic attacks and has adopted a dramatically different pace of life.
"This is my life. I get to enjoy time," she said. "I sit down and eat lunch. I sit down and talk to people. There's no phones on the tables."
"There’s a grace given for enjoyment in life," Esposito continued. "I just think we've lost the plot with that. And no wonder why we're all sick."
Looking back on the ordeal, Esposito said she ultimately views her diagnosis as something that changed the trajectory of her life.
"Celiac disease saved my life. One hundred percent," she said.
Esposito said she believes the years of stress and living in "fight or flight" would eventually have taken an even greater toll had her illness not forced her to change course.
"I 100% would have been somewhere not good," she said.

title: ‘This Is Us’ star Chrissy Metz says she turned to GLP-1 drug after years of skepticism
summary: Chrissy Metz says she was "nervous and scared" to try a GLP-1 but her doctor recommended it, and she's now focused on longevity and overall health.
story: Ethan Suplee reflects on the ongoing responsibility that comes with becoming a public weight-loss success story and explains why consistent support from like-minded people keeps him on track.
Chrissy Metz is opening up about her decision to use a GLP-1 after years of skepticism about the popular weight-loss medications.

During an appearance on the "Today" show on Monday, the "This Is Us" star, 45, explained that she reconsidered the drugs as she entered perimenopause and thought more seriously about her health and her family's history with obesity.
"I was very skeptical about GLP-1s for years," she said. "I had a friend who was like, I don't know, he gave me a thesis, and I was like, 'OK, this might be helpful.'"
MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS
Chrissy Metz said that she's started taking weight-loss medication. (Getty Images for A+E Global Media)
After witnessing her father experience complications with his own health, Metz thought, "Maybe I should try and get ahead of it."
"It was something that I thought would be good for me," she said.
Since taking the drug, Metz said she's noticed a difference in her energy level, as well as her "overall health."
Despite the previous skepticism, Metz said the most important thing for her is "longevity."

"Learning what it really was and how it affects everybody differently ... my doctor and my team were like, ‘Yeah, I think this would be beneficial for you,’" said Metz, who admitted she was "nervous" and "scared" to try it.

Metz admitted she was "nervous" to try taking a GLP-1. (Rodin Eckenroth)

It's good for me because I'm really putting myself first. It's something I've always wanted to do, but I have to really put into practice now."

"It's been a really wonderful journey," she added.

Metz is best known for starring in "This Is Us." (Getty Images)
