title: Harry Jowsey’s Reality Show Ends in a Real Wedding. Here’s Who He Marries
summary: Who does Harry Jowsey marry in the finale of Let’s Marry Harry? What happens in the finale?
story: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “Let’s Marry Harry.”

Twenty engagement rings later, Netflix heartthrob Harry Jowsey started the “Let’s Marry Harry” finale with two fiancés left and one difficult decision to make. And for much of the episode, it wasn’t clear he would make one at all.

The end of Episode 7 saw the “Too Hot to Handle” and “Perfect Match” star alone and emotional on the beach after visiting his family in New Zealand with his two finalists, Dannelle Davidson and Amber Mozo.
Sam Kruse, who rounded out Harry’s final three, made a sudden exit from the show at the start of Episode 7 after a series of conversations with Harry didn’t go to plan.

Despite only being a couple of days out from the altar, Harry started Episode 8, the finale, with no clarity about which of the two women he would say “I do” to. And to his close friends and members of his trusty support (and selection) squad, Sonny Henty and Amanda Kloots, he suggested a new option: abandoning both women altogether.

But ultimately, Harry did make a choice between Dannelle, 33-year-old cocktail waitress from Las Vegas, and Amber, 30-year-old travel photographer from Hawaii — one that brought all three of them to tears.
Read on to learn who Harry chose to spend forever with.
Who Does Harry Jowsey Marry in the ‘Let’s Marry Harry’ Finale?
With Dannelle all made up in her wedding glam and gown, Harry knocked on the door and sat down with her for a conversation.
Although he told Dannelle he’d fallen in love with her, he also said that he had “started second guessing everything,” and that the two were not going to get married.

“I don’t think you deserve someone that will second guess you, the person should know 100% and shouldn’t be worried about everything,” he told Dannelle. “I know that you deserve that at the bare minimum.”
“I thought it was something else this whole time with us but apparently it wasn’t,” she responded, in part. “I just feel stupid.”
After saying goodbye to one bride, Harry geared up to wait at the end of the aisle for his other one: Amber.

The Australian heartthrob became emotional immediately upon seeing Amber in her white dress, and the tears kept flowing throughout the ceremony as they gushed about their love throughout their vows — Harry’s pre-written and Amber’s spontaneous.

“You’re a miracle, and I know our dads are probably best friends up there,” Harry told Amber as he wore a pair of his dad’s glasses, whose memory he honored throughout the season. “You’re not just someone I fell for, you’re someone who makes me grow and look at life different.”
“I’m wearing these glasses because I want my dad to see how beautiful you are,” he added.
“Ending up here with you in this way is the best thing that’s ever happened to me,” Amber told Harry.
After they tied the knot, the night carried on with a celebratory reception packed with the bride and groom’s friends and family.
In a subsequent flashback sequence captured two weeks after the wedding, the newlyweds looked as in love as ever, enjoying beach days and time in bed.
Are Harry Jowsey and Amber Mozo Still Together Now?

Speculation about the couple’s current status has unfolded online since Amber posted an Instagram story in July on the shoulders of a man who doesn’t look like Harry. Neither Harry or Amber has publicly addressed their current relationship status.
The “Let’s Marry Harry” reunion is set to premiere Aug. 26.

title: ‘No Influencers’ Sign At Nantucket Craft Shop Sparks Massive Internet Debate
summary: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.

Nantucket has always been one of the most picturesque vacation spots in Massachusetts. But one small business on the island has sparked controversy for seemingly drawing a line in the sand, discouraging one particular group of tourists from visiting.

Four Winds Craft Guild, a store that sells handmade arts and crafts, recently installed a sign that reads “No Influencers,” inspiring a heated debate when they shared a photo of the sign on Instagram. Fans of the sign say it’s a cheeky reaction to the rise of influencer culture, while critics say it’s dismissive of social media content creators, many of whom are women.
John Sylvia, the owner of the store, told The New York Times that the sign was meant to be “tongue-in-cheek” and a reference to the rising popularity of influencer culture.
“I feel sometimes my store is used as someone’s background, a stage,” he said.
When Sylvia’s partner, Jessica Jenkins, initially shared a photo of the sign on Instagram, many influencers had strong feelings about the post. The social media platform later removed it.
How are fans and critics of the sign reacting? NBC’s Kaylee Hartung explored the brewing controversy in a segment for TODAY. Here’s everything you need to know.
Why Did the Shop Put Up a ‘No Influencers’ Sign?
In an interview with The New York Times, Sylvia said the sign wasn’t intended to be an attack on influencers.
“I don’t have this hatred toward influencers,” he said. “It was more of a joke. It is a problem we should look at as a society.”
The shop owner went on to say that many visitors come into the store to take photos and videos for social media and don’t speak to him or make purchases.
After Instagram removed the shop’s post, Jenkins shared a second post on July 27 with the following cheeky caption: “TAKE TWO 🎬.”

While speaking with The New York Times, Jenkins, a year-round resident on the island, described how influencers have impacted the culture on Nantucket. For starters, she said she notices an influx of “people creating videos on corners of themselves sipping an iced coffee and looking over their shoulder and doing a shoe kick or whatever.”
“I feel that whenever I open Instagram, I see someone show me a guide of what to wear, a guide of where to eat, a guide of what to buy, a guide of how to pack for Nantucket,” she said.

Nantucket has faced increased tourism over the years, with long lines at businesses. Former “Real Housewives of New York City” star and influencer Bethenny Frankel said in a social media video Aug. 1 the island has become an “absolute zoo.”
According to Nantucket’s government website, the island has a year-round population of around 11,000 but peaks in July and August to more than 50,000.
Why Is the ‘No Influencers’ Sign So Controversial?
The shop’s post instantly drew criticism from many influencers.
“How stupid can you be to put a sign in a store that prohibits basically free marketing?” TikTok user @kristinacanale asked in a recent video.
TikTok user @ivyynielsen shared a similar sentiment, saying, “It sent the message that creators aren’t welcome, and I don’t think that’s fair.”
Instagram user @levicoralynn offered the following take in a video, saying, “I think hating influencers has become a socially acceptable way to hate women.”
Though Four Winds Craft Guild made no mention of women in its sign, women make up a large percentage of lifestyle influencers, leading some critics to interpret the sign as an attack on women.
Lifestyle creator Paige Lorenze, who opened a boutique in Nantucket earlier this summer, commented on the original Instagram post, saying the sign was an attempt to “delegitimize” and “mock” women.
“It’s just a strange message coming from a store that celebrates a craft with such a rich history of women shaping the island and its economy,” she wrote.
But despite the backlash, some social media users saw the humor in the sign.
“This sign is funny!” Instagram user @lawyerlimor said in a video. “It’s funny!”
TikTok user @thedanahaffner shared the following reaction: “What happened to humor?? It’s just a little bit of like local humor.”
TikTok user @tiesyn supported the shop owner in a video, saying, “Don’t come in here acting entitled. More stores need to have a sign like that.”
Others Areas Have Attempted to Restrict Influencers
The rise of influencer tourism has led some vacation destinations to place restrictions on visitors in recent years.
In 2023, neighbors living near Sleepy Hollow Farm in Vermont created a petition to close nearby roads and prevent influencers from inundating the streets to snap photos of fall foliage.
One island in Finland also declared itself phone-free and started giving tourists stickers to cover their screens in an effort to help them enjoy nature.

Portofino on the Italian Riviera established “no-waiting zones” in 2023, with potential fines up to €275 to curb what the town’s mayor called “anarchic chaos” — tourists stopping to take selfies, per the BBC.

title: After Landing ‘Rockford Files’ Reboot Role, David Boreanaz Asked James Garner’s Daughter for Her Blessing
summary: David Boreanaz shared what he told James Garner’s daughter, Gigi Garner, after he was cast to lead NBC’s reboot of “The Rockford Files.”
story: When David Boreanaz learned he would lead NBC’s reboot of “The Rockford Files,” he knew he had to reach out to James Garner’s daughter, Gigi Garner, to receive her “blessing.”

The 57-year-old actor has been a constant on network television for decades, with starring roles on “Buffy the Vampire Slayer,” “Angel,” “Bones” and “SEAL Team.” But soon he will take on a new challenge as he inherits James Garner’s iconic role of Jim Rockford, a Los Angeles private investigator who relies on unconventional means to solve his crimes. James Garner, who died on July 19, 2014 at the age of 86, played the character on the original NBC series for six seasons from 1974 to 1980.

At NBC’s Backlot Pass 2026 event on Aug. 10 previewing the network and Peacock’s fall and midseason lineup, Boreanaz spoke about being inspired by the late actor, which made him want to contact Gigi Garner to assure her that her father’s legacy was in good hands.
During a panel conversation with “The Rockford Files” writer and executive producer Mike Daniels, Boreanaz explained how he got in touch with Gigi Garner to inform her of the casting news.

He said he has known the author and singer for over 15 years. He previously purchased a pinball machine from her that was a prop on her father’s show “Maverick.” But, the two had lost touch over the years. After landing the role, he found Gigi Garner’s old email address and decided to send her a message.
“I was like, I’m just going to give it a shot. I sent the email out and, to my surprise, she replied back. And I said, ‘I have to have a conversation with you,’” he recalled.
They chatted on the phone and he told her about the reboot.

“And she said, ‘Yeah, OK. I don’t know who’s going to play my father.’ And I said, ‘Well, they offered me the role,’” he continued. “And the first thing I said to her is, ‘A, I need your blessing. But first and foremost, I’m not going to play what your father did. What your father did is iconic and he’s already climbed that mountaintop. I inspire to do the same with this character, but I’m not imitating him.’”
In fact, Boreanaz told the panel audience that he didn’t grow up a fan of “The Rockford Files” and had never seen an episode.
He emphasized to Gigi Garner that he only had one goal: to make her dad proud.
“That’s it. Simple and clean and do the work,” he told her.
After they hung up, he said he went for a swim and thanked James Garner.

“I know that he’s with us. I know that he was with us in the pilot. I understand that’s a little too esoteric to think of, but that’s who I am as a person. I believe in that. I believe (the) universe has brought us to this specific moment and I do believe he’s with us,” he shared.

Another important figure in Boreanaz’s life who he has been thinking about as he enters the next chapter of his career is his mother. He said a “piece of him” owes the “Rockford” role to her because she pointed out the “uncanny” resemblance between him and James Garner years ago.
Boreanaz shared that when he was working on “Bones” his mother told him he needed to find a project connected to “The Great Escape” star.
“My mother’s spirit obviously brought that to light, somehow. So I thank my mom a little bit for that energy,” he added.
While executive producer Daniels also noted the similarities between Boreanaz and James Garner, he said the two share more characteristics that made him the perfect actor for the reboot.

“David obviously has a resemblance to Garner, but there are moments in this pilot and moments when we were on set shooting it that he would suddenly look in the camera and it was just uncanny,” Daniels said. “It wasn’t just the features. It was the half smile, the charm, the smirk, the twinkle behind the eye. It just suddenly all fit.”

He added, “Certainly, when we cast him, we were like, ‘Oh, great. He even kind of looks like the guy,’ you know. And then he got on set and we were like, ‘Whoa, he feels like the guy too in how he’s inhabiting this character.”

NBC announced it greenlit a contemporary reboot of “The Rockford Files” with Boreanaz in a press release in May. The show is expected to premiere in January 2027, with an exact date to be announced this fall. Joining Boreanaz will be Academy Award nominee Jacki Weaver, Michaela McManus and Felix Solis.

The logline for the series will sound familiar to fans of the original: “Newly paroled after doing time for a crime he didn’t commit, James Rockford returns to his life as a private investigator using his charm and wit to solve cases around Los Angeles. It doesn’t take long for his quest for legitimacy to land him squarely in the crosshairs of both local police and organized crime.”
However, Daniels clarified at the panel that the show will not be a “one‑for‑one, apples‑to‑apples remake.”

“I think you can kind of get in trouble with people who are sentimental with the original. It just becomes a comparison: who is the actor they remember loving as a kid and who’s the actor playing it now,” he explained.
Instead, he said he hopes to recapture the feeling fans experienced when they watched the classic.

title: Sugarland Is Taking Breakout Album ‘Enjoy the Ride’ Back on Tour for 20th Anniversary
summary: Sugarland is hitting the road for their “Ride Or Die Tour” for a very special reason: the 20th anniversary of their breakout album “Enjoy the Ride.”
story: Sugarland is hitting the road for a very special reason.
To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their hit album “Enjoy the Ride,” the country duo is heading out on tour this fall.

On Aug. 11, Jennifer Nettles and Kristian Bush sat down with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones to discuss their exciting announcement and give a preview of what fans can expect from the aptly named the “Ride Or Die Tour.”

Nettles and Bush will be touring cities across the country from Oct. 1 to Nov. 21 to celebrate the album that solidified their spot as country icons. The official Instagram account for the duo released the official lineup of dates Aug. 11. Ticket presale begins Aug. 12 at 10 a.m. followed by general onsale Aug. 14.

Following its 2006 release, “Enjoy the Ride” went triple platinum. Throughout their time as a band, Sugarland has sold nearly 10 million albums in the U.S. The duo has won two Grammy Awards,  five ACM Awards and five consecutive CMA Awards for vocal duo of the year, from 2007 to 2011.
Nettles specifically points to “Enjoy the Ride” as a “turning point” in their career.
“Our debut album was great, but then this (was) really like when people started to really catch on to what we were doing and like it,” she said.

Bush said the album holds a special place in Sugarland’s heart since it was the first one they produced together. Outside of the band, Bush himself has produced an endless amount of music for other artists.
“Dreaming up how things sound and how they feel, it’s something I’ve been doing my whole life,” he said.
Looking back on their band’s enduring success, Nettles said she has “so much gratitude,” and Bush echoed her sentiments.
After collaborating for several decades, Bush and Nettles have a simple secret for forming a successful working relationship that lasts.

“I think like any relationship, you keep it fresh and you communicate. It doesn’t matter if it’s family. It doesn’t matter if it’s intimate. It doesn’t matter if it’s creative. Whatever, like keep it fresh. We do obviously other things. Kristian’s a fantastic producer (and) has hit records out the wazoo with Megan Moroney right now,” Nettles said.
Bush added that he and Nettles are a “unique duo” for one particular reason.

“Almost every single time we’ve sat down to do anything, maybe even in the dressing room before we walked up here, we will come up with ideas on the spot that work almost every time. And I don’t know what that (is), you know, I grab onto her,” he said.

Before announcing their new tour, Sugarland teased some exciting news on their Instagram account, posting a video of the country duo taking a bow on stage. The band captioned the post, “It’s been a minute...” and added the words “Coming soon” to the end of the video.

The day before announcing their tour, Sugarland shared another video of Nettles and Bush performing. As a plethora of excited fan comments appeared in the video, the words “We hear you!” could be seen at the end of the short clip.
Sugarland added fuel to the fire, captioning the post, “Don’t miss out...”

Sugarland released their last album in 2018 with “Bigger,” reuniting after going on hiatus starting in 2012. Nettles and Bush last toured together as Sugarland in 2024, co-headlining the “Take Me Home Tour” with Little Big Town.

title: QVC’s Toni Brattin Says She ‘Froze’ After That Viral Mishap: ‘I Just Went Down!’
summary: Jimmy Fallon had a visit from QVC wig mogul Tami Brattin days after her viral moment.
story: Jimmy Fallon’s comedic take on a viral QVC on-air moment has viewers wigging out.
The host of “The Tonight Show” welcomed TV personality Toni Brattin to his show Aug. 10 and spoofed an embarrassing moment she experienced during a recent QVC segment.
In case you missed the hilarious moment, Brattin was showcasing her collection of wigs on air when she accidentally made a NSFW reference.
While describing the wig she was wearing, Brattin said, “It looks like you went and got a blowjob.” She quickly self-corrected, saying, “a blowout at your salon.”
Terri Conn, a QVC host who was also present for the segment, quickly intervened and reminded viewers that they could take advantage of a “huge beauty sale.”
As Conn began to speak, Brattin shook her head and lowered herself to the floor, out of the camera frame.

After viewing the awkward on-air moment, Fallon poked fun at it during an episode of “The Tonight Show” last week, saying, “Note to all the married men out there: The wig is only available on your birthday, apparently.”
When Brattin saw the clip, she applauded Fallon for his witty comment during an interview with TMZ.

“Jimmy, hat’s off. I had to laugh at him as much as I had to laugh at myself. I happened to save one of those wigs just for Jimmy and I would love to see what this wig would look like on Jimmy. So Jimmy, you just tell me when your birthday is and I’ll hand deliver this and we’ll see how cute you look in it,” she said.
Brattin kept her promise and appeared on “The Tonight Show” Aug. 10.
Fallon set the scene for the segment, saying, “My birthday is actually coming up.”
Brattin then appeared and waved a brown wig in the air.
“I think that you handled that perfectly, by the way. You really nailed it,” Fallon told Brattin of her viral moment.
The TV host then asked the QVC personality what she was thinking as she slowly sank out of the camera frame after her on-air flub.
“Well, you know, I was kind of froze(n) and I was trying to decide, ‘Do I go to the left? Do I go to the right?’ I just went down,” she said.
Brattin then showed Fallon the brown wig she selected for him and put it on his head.
“Oh, look at all that hair!” she said.
“Yeah, you love it?” Fallon replied.
“And how about the volume in the back?” she added.
“Oh yeah. I love it,” Fallon said, then posed. “I’m honored. I love it.”
Brattin paused to fluff up the wig a bit then covered her face and laughed as Fallon exclaimed, “I am blown away.”
The duo ended the segment by turning their backs to the camera and lowering their bodies as they introduced “The Tonight Show” house band, The Roots.

title: Usher Responds to Rumors as Fans Believe He’s Hired a Look-Alike to Perform at Concerts
summary: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
story: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
Fans have been doing double takes for days after footage from a recent “The R&B Tour” concert has convinced many of them that the man performing on stage was a fake.

Sunnya Sultan, who saw the tour in person Aug. 7 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, shared a TikTok video questioning if the 47-year-old “Yeah” singer was truly the one dancing in front of her.
The performer wears a white with lime green and pink ensemble, ball cap and sunglasses as he sings and dances.
Sultan tells TODAY.com she believes she did see Usher perform. She’s also convinced an Usher look-alike also took the stage during a portion of the show.

“Usher came out. The real Usher came out but then he sang like half a song, maybe for like 40 seconds,” Sultan recalls. “Then he goes into this darkness and he comes out, and as he’s walking, I think everyone really thought that was Usher.”
“But as the first song finishes, I think everyone started getting confused because the way he was moving wasn’t really Usher,” she continues.

When she looked closely, she believed something was off about the Usher who now appeared onstage. She noted that his jawline that was “a little too chiseled” and the performer “seemed a little too stiff.”
Also, he was dressed differently. The “real” Usher, she says, came out shirtless and wearing a fur coat.
The Usher who later performed in front of her, she adds, was “fully covered,” as seen in her TikTok video.
“Everything was just kind of weird,” Sultan says. “He looked like him, and then at certain angles he definitely did not look like him.”
Sultan said concertgoers all around her were suspicious.
Usher addressed the rumors in a video posted on the tour’s official Instagram Aug. 9.
“Usure? Wesure,” reads the caption.
The video showed Usher performing onstage in the same white ensemble. It also included screenshots of Usher replying to comments made about the alleged imposter.
“Ya’ll are funny…clone? They can’t clone this??” the singer wrote alongside a laughing emoji.
“How ya’ll come up with this? AI ain’t that advanced,” he added along with more laughing emoji.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Has Shocking Elimination After Dancer Failed to Deliver ‘Wow Moment’
summary: Who was eliminated on ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ episode 5? The Aug. 10 episode saw a shocking elimination after one dancer failed to deliver a “wow moment.”
story: The competition continues on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” and now it’s time to shine.
In the Aug. 10 episode of the “Dancing With the Stars” spinoff, pro Daniella Karagach showed off her impressive skills with a mega performance as host Robert Irwin introduced the challenge.

This week it was all about having that “wow” moment that “DWTS” viewers love. The six remaining dancers were mentored and guided by Daniella as they created a contemporary routine that incorporated one of her signature and viral moves.
If the dancers failed to deliver a spectacular move in their choreographer, they would be at risk for elimination. But first, the contestants took a trip to the Australia Zoo for inspiration.
What Happened During Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’

When Daniella entered the rehearsal room, she told the dancers that they also had to create their own standout moment that would “forever be embedded in someone’s memory.” This was in addition to including one of Daniella’s “wow” moves.
“The more you wow the audience, the longer you and your partner stay in the competition,” she said about competing on “DWTS.”

Since last week, the ladies got to choose their partners, this week the guys picked who they wanted to perform with. If more than one guy chose the same girl, she would have the option to choose who she wanted to partner up with.
Allen Genkin chose Adele Zaikman, while AJ Pritchard and Erik Linder chose Selena Hamilton. No one chose Nina Mayster.
Selena ultimately chose Erik, meaning AJ and Nina would be partners by default.

AJ and Nina were up first, performing a contemporary piece to “Human” by Christina Perri that impressed the judges. Daniella told them they “understood the assignment,” while judge Mark Ballas complimented their “total trust.”
Shirley Ballas also applauded their multiple wow moments, AJ’s vulnerability and Nina’s musicality.
Next were Allen and Adele, who also got major kudos from the judges with their routine to “All That Really Matters” by Illenium featuring Teddy Swims.
Mark was a fan of their wow moments, that included the Allen-copter and caveman walk at the beginning. He also called Adele a “diamond.”
Shirley echoed her son’s comments, calling her “beyond a diamond, one of the best female dancers I’ve ever seen.” Daniella also shared how she loved the routine.
Last but not least were Erik and Selena, who specializes in contemporary, with a routine to “You Stole the Show” by Sienna Spiro.
Shirley began her comments by saying she was “conflicted” and didn’t know what their wow moment was. Selena replied that sometimes the “wow” is in the silence.
Shirley continued by saying she would have liked to see Erik let go more and ultimately wasn’t impressed. While she did appreciate the quality of Selena’s routine, she expected more.
Mark and Daniella both shared kind words about their dancing, but noted that they did not follow direction.
Who Was in the Bottom 2?
Because they did not complete the challenge and include a visibly “wow moment” in their routine, Erik and Selena were on the chopping block.
The other four contestants were visibly emotional in the background, as Daniella said, “If you have a challenge, you have to deliver it. You have to make that the priority.”
Who Got Eliminated on Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
Ultimately, Shirley shared that with a “very, very heavy heart” this would be the last dance for Erik.
Allen broke down in tears, with Adele and Nina covering their faces in shock.
Shirley told Erik that he was “a beautiful dancer,” but applauded Selena for her strong and advanced choreography.

“I knew that I was taking a risk,” Erik said in his confessional, adding that he didn’t regret a single decision that he made. He then thanked the judges for the opportunity to grow as a dancer and person.
What Will Happen Next Week?
Five dancers remain on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.” For the Aug. 17 episode, guest judge Witney Carson will deliver the dancers’ toughest challenge yet: teaching ballroom novice.
In the next episode, the contestants will be paired with “DWTS” superfans who are dancing amateurs. They will then have two days to prepare a performance that will land them a spot in the semifinals.

title: Brad Pitt Makes Rare Comment About ‘Pain’ of ‘Family Stuff’
summary: In a new interview, Brad Pitt shares that he’s never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”
story: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.
In a rare mention of his personal life, Brad Pitt says in a new interview that he has never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”

The 62-year-old Hollywood icon made a short reference to his family situation in an interview with Esquire published on Aug. 10  in which he talked about “oppressive” pain that led him to a dark place where he could “understand suicide.”
In the Esquire interview, Pitt initially shared his thoughts about going to dark places in life, unconnected to any question about his family.
“I was never suicidal in any way,” he said. “It just was not my makeup. In fact, if I have any afflictions, it’s probably being a congenital optimist,” he said.
He reiterated he’s “never been suicidal,” before adding, “except for one little period.”

“And in that one little period, I just thought — I just couldn’t — just didn’t see a way out,” he said. “The pain was so oppressive that — I wasn’t going to act on this, but I could feel — I could feel the cold steel of the bullet in my head, and it felt like relief. And I thought, Oh, okay, now I understand — I understand suicide, in the sense that it’s just relief. It’s just looking for relief from the pain. But I also think we have incredible survival instincts. And for me, that immediately kicked in, but it was just ...”
Pitt was asked what could have provoked him to think about suicide in that way. The reporter questioned if it was “kid stuff,” per the Esquire article.
“Family stuff,” Pitt said. “We could leave it at that.”

Pitt and his ex-wife, Angelina Jolie, have six children. The couple reached a divorce settlement in 2024 after Jolie accused Pitt of verbal and physical abuse, which he has denied. Their daughter Shiloh, 20, legally dropped “Pitt” from her last name when she turned 18 in 2024. Two of his other children have also considered ditching “Pitt” from their last name, according to a court filing in California cited by CNN in July 2026.
The “F1” star was later asked how he endured the difficult period he referenced.

“I don’t see it as climbing out of it,” he said. “It’s going through it and trying and trying and trying and trying to the point of exhaustion and then trying again. I don’t want to ignore the place where you run up against the wall. But I just one day woke up, and it just felt a little sunnier and the air felt a little sweeter. Just microdoses of it.”

Pitt does not make it clear in the interview what “little period” he is referring to in his life. Elsewhere in the interview, he discussed the death of his mother in August 2025 and said, referencing his father, “Let’s just say it’s better to be the one who goes first.”
Once Hollywood’s most famous couple, Pitt, and Jolie, 51, met on the set of the 2005 movie “Mr. & Mrs. Smith” and got married in 2014. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016.

In 2022, amid already contentious divorce proceedings, Jolie accused Pitt of physical and verbal abuse on a 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles, during which he allegedly choked one of their children, which prompted her to file for divorce, according to a court filing from Jolie.
“Brad has owned everything he’s responsible for from day one — unlike the other side — but he’s not going to own anything he didn’t do,” a lawyer for Pitt said in 2022.

No criminal charges were ever filed against Pitt. In 2016, both the FBI and the Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services closed an investigation into allegations of abuse onboard the flight.

The acrimony since their split has also included Pitt filing a lawsuit in 2022 accusing Jolie of intentionally harming him and the French winery business they once shared by selling her stake in it. The former couple purchased shares in the 148-acre French vineyard Chateau Miraval together in 2008.

Following Pitt’s lawsuit about the winery, Jolie filed the 2022 cross-complaint that alleged Pitt subjected their family to verbal and physical abuse aboard the aforementioned 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles.
Their divorce was settled in 2024, and the dispute over the winery remains ongoing.

title: Romy Reiner’s Latest TV Role Has a Touching Tie to Her Late Dad, Rob Reiner
summary: Romy Reiner appeared in the finale of Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness,” which her dad Rob Reiner also appeared in.
story: Romy Reiner followed in her late father Rob Reiner’s footsteps by appearing on Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness.”
The elder Reiner made a posthumous cameo in the sketch show in an episode that aired July 3, months after his shocking death. He played George Washington.
Romy Reiner, meanwhile, guest-starred in the series finale on Aug. 7 as a nurse caring for President William Henry Harrison (Fred Melamed).
Romy Reiner’s appearance comes five years after she got her big break in 2021 playing a cashier on David’s HBO series “Curb Your Enthusiasm.” David was one of Rob Reiner’s close friends.
The 28-year-old actor is the youngest child of the legendary actor and director and his late wife Michele Singer.
The couple, who were married for 36 years, were found fatally stabbed at home on Dec. 14, 2025, according to the L.A. district attorney’s office.
Their youngest son, Nick Reiner, 32, was arrested and charged Dec. 16 with two counts of first degree murder. In February, Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to the charges.
The Reiners also shared an older son, Jake Reiner, 35, who posted a heartbreaking tribute to his parents in an April 24 post on Substack.
Rob Reiner was also the father of an adoptive daughter, Tracy Reiner, with his ex-wife, actor and director Penny Marshall.
In his essay on Substack, Jake Reiner revealed he was at a friend’s celebration of life in Los Angeles when his sister called to tell him their parents were dead.

“The 45-minute Lyft ride from downtown to the west side was unendurable,” he wrote. “My world, as I knew it, had collapsed. I was in a trance. The only thing I could focus on was that I needed to get to my childhood home. I needed to get to my sister. I needed to figure out what the hell just happened.”
Jake Reiner wrote about his grief that his parents won’t be alive to witness future milestones in his life.

“My parents won’t be at my wedding, they won’t get to hold their future grandchild, and they won’t get to see me have the successful career I’m still seeking,” he wrote. “It simultaneously breaks my heart and enrages me.”
Rob Reiner, who was 78 when he died, was the son of comedy legend Carl Reiner. He found fame in the early 1970s playing Michael “Meathead” Stivic on the sitcom “All in the Family.”

He went on to become one of Hollywood’s most beloved directors, helming the cult classic “This Is Spinal Tap” as well as the box office hits “Stand By Me,” “The Princess Bride,” “When Harry Met Sally,” “Misery” and “A Few Good Men.”
He married photographer and producer Michele Reiner in May 1989.
In his essay, Jake Reiner called his parents “the most giving people.” He described his father as his “hero” and Singer as “the backbone” of the family.
Losing his parents together in such a violent manner — with his brother “at the center of it” — has been, he wrote, a “living nightmare.”

title: New Yorker Accidentally Threw Away 2 Family Rings. 20,000 Pounds of Trash Later, They Were Recovered
summary: New York City sanitation workers dug through 20,000 pounds of garbage to ensure that one man’s trash didn’t also mean the loss of his treasure.
story: New York City sanitation workers dug through 20,000 pounds of garbage to ensure that one man’s trash didn’t also mean the loss of his treasure.
A Brooklyn man is breathing a massive sigh of relief after he accidentally threw a pair of priceless family rings in the garbage at a large residential building last month.

The ring’s owner realized the mistake before the trash was picked up, so he met sanitation workers at the curb on July 28 to explain the predicament, a spokesperson for the New York City Department of Sanitation told TODAY.com in an email statement.
The heirloom rings were a gold-and-diamond promise ring and platinum-and-diamond engagement ring that had been in the family for four generations, according to the DSNY.

Sanitation workers were able to isolate the truck and slowly dump the nearly 20,000 pounds of trash across a concrete floor to be searched. After only 10 minutes, the rings were found to the relief and joy of the resident, whose name was withheld by the DSNY.
“It isn’t exactly a needle in a haystack, but some accidentally discarded rings were dug up!,” the DSNY wrote on Facebook.
“Can you imagine?” Savannah Guthrie said on TODAY Aug. 10. “Out of the goodness of their hearts being like, ‘I’m going to sift through 20,000 pounds of trash,’ and they found it! Incredible.”
The DSNY spokesperson said searches like that happen multiple times a year, and there is a process for them.

Any residents who accidentally throw out a valuable item are urged to call 311 as soon as possible. After each call, sanitation workers aim to isolate the truck and slowly dump the contents on a concrete floor to be sifted through.

The timeliness of the call is crucial. If a truck has already dumped the trash at a transfer station, there’s no way to recover the lost item because it’s usually immediately mixed with trash from other trucks to be put into a barge or railcar.

The resident is allowed to participate in the search for his or her item and can bring one friend to help. The DSNY provides gloves, shovels, pickers and other tools for the search while also sharing possible spots to look. For instance, if the person’s address was at the beginning of the sanitation truck’s route, the material may be more near the back of the truck.
The recovery of the Brooklyn man’s rings is the latest success story for the DSNY, which has previously found everything from a wallet to a laptop that had been accidentally tossed out.
“Way to go New York City Sanitation,” Craig Melvin said on TODAY.

title: Anthony Bourdain’s Daughter Was A ‘Brutal’ Critic About His Cooking, He Joked In 2016 on TODAY
summary: In 2016, Anthony Bourdain sat down with TODAY’s Willie Geist to reflect on how he got into TV, his experiences traveling the world and cooking for his daughter.
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Anthony Bourdain’s conversation with Willie Geist on Oct. 23, 2016.
The legacy of Anthony Bourdain lives on with the release of “Tony,”
In the film, out now, Dominic Sessa plays the celebrated and complicated chef, who died in 2018 at the age of 61 by suicide, leaving behind a legion of fans who are still inspired by him.

In 2016, Bourdain sat down with Sunday TODAY’s Willie Geist to reflect on his career, remembering how he wound up a fixture of the small screen, what it was like to eat with the president and how his toughest critic may be his daughter.
How Did Anthony Bourdain Break Into Show Business?

Bourdain shot to stardom after he wrote the 2000 book “Kitchen Confidential,” which, based on his experience, took readers behind the scenes of the restaurant industry. It also touched on his personal struggles with addiction.
“I wrote an article,” he told Willie at the time. “My mom actually said, ‘You should send it to the New Yorker.’”
“The next day I got a call saying, ‘You know, we’ll give you 50 grand to write a book,’” he recalled. “I’m no dummy, I’m dunking french fries at age 44. I’ll write the d--- book.”
What Was Next for Bourdain After That?

The next stop was television. Following stints on the Travel Channel and Food Network, Bourdain turned his success into the long-running TV series “Parts Unknown,” in which he dove into the food of obscure places around the globe.

“Some delusional crackpots walked into the restaurant and offered me a TV show, and they showed up reeking of garlic, with a really bad attitude,” he recalled about how he wound up making shows about food and travel.

“I said, ‘I got a great idea. I travel around the world doing whatever I want in every cool place I ever dreamed of, and you pay. How’s that idea?’” he said. “And they were like, ‘Sounds like ... yeah. We’ll take 13 (episodes) of those.”
Bourdain Was Curious About Traveling Around the World
Bourdain was not afraid to get out of his comfort zone when it came to where he would visit.
“I’m not going full Geraldo (Rivera) out there in my flak jacket, poking my head up over a foxhole,” he said.
“But, you know, I’m curious about the world. And if there are manageable risks in return for satisfying my curiosity about a place, I’m willing,” he shared.
He Ate With Former President Barack Obama
Bourdain did sit down once with Barack Obama while he was president and remembered how he handled a potentially tricky question when he asked Obama how he felt about eating a hot dog with ketchup.

“Most people running for office would say, ‘Both ketchup and mustard, there are virtues, and I respect and admire people who...’ you know, get some wishy-washy answer to not piss off all the ketchup people. He said, ‘No, never!’” Bourdain recalled.
How Did Bourdain Choose Which Places to Spotlight?
For Bourdain, visiting an eatery, even if no one was familiar with it, came down to something very simple.

“The kind of questions we’re asking is, ‘Look, what does your soul crave at 2 o’clock in the morning when you got a little bit of a buzz?’ More often than not, that goes right to the heart of the culture,” he said.
Bourdain’s Daughter Was Not Afraid to Criticize His Cooking

Bourdain shared a daughter, Ariane, with ex-wife Ottavia Busia. She was 11 when he died, and Bourdain told Willie in their 2016 chat that she was tough as nails when it came to her reviews of his food.
“She’s brutal. I cannot get anything past her,” he said. “It’s like, ‘No, daddy, it’s too salty.’ ‘No, it’s not.’ Secretly, I know, yeah, she caught me. Every time.”
At the time, he also spoke about how his daughter inspired his new cookbook “Appetites: A Cookbook.”

title: ‘Wicker’ Movie Explained: Why Is the Internet Thirsting Over a Sentient Basket?
summary: What is the Wicker movie? Here’s the explanation of the Wicker movie, what it’s based on and the reaction to it.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the biggest headlines, leading with your questions. In this latest series, we’re breaking down why a movie about love and wicker sparked a big reaction.
The Scarecrow and the Tin Man better watch out, because there’s a new anthropomorphic leading man who has captured Hollywood’s attention … and he’s made of wicker.

Distributor Black Bear Pictures delighted and bewildered the internet on July 30 when it released the first trailer for an upcoming romantic fantasy comedy titled “Wicker,” out in theaters in the U.S. Oct. 23 and Oct. 30 in the UK. (The movie premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival in January.)

The film was first announced back in October 2023, when Variety reported that Oscar-winner Olivia Colman and Dev Patel were attached to a movie featuring an “unconventional romance.” But two years later, the publication announced Alexander Skarsgård would replace Patel, and that Peter Dinklage and Elizabeth Debicki were joining the cast, too.

A star-studded cast plus an intriguing plot seem like a recipe for a film worth checking out. But nothing could have prepared the internet for the first look, which showed Skarsgård’s full transformation into an unrecognizable man made of wicker.
Read on to find out why the internet is thirsting over Skarsgård’s twine-filled alter ego.
What Is ‘Wicker’ About?

As the film title implies, wicker is at the center of the story. The nearly two-and-a-half minute NSFW teaser that Black Bear Pictures debuted, which has already amassed over 1.5 million views, welcomes viewers to a seaside village where a fisherwoman, played by Colman, is ridiculed by members of the town.
Lonely and in need of a companion, the fisherwoman visits a local craftsman, portrayed by Dinklage, and requests that he make her a husband.
“Be at the chapel in a month,” he simply tells her.

After bending and molding endless sticks of twine, he creates her husband: Skarsgård’s wicker man. From head to toe, he is covered in wicker strands, which have been weaved and stitched together in various patterns across his body.
“I’m here to marry you,” Skarsgård’s character tells the fisherwoman upon seeing her. It’s safe to say she is pleased with the results.
The two begin their unusual love story, as some of the townspeople who previously mocked the fisherwoman now desire the same romance. Others are mortified and chaos ensues.
What Inspired ‘Wicker’?

“Wicker” was adapted from Ursula Wills-Jones’ short story “The Wicker Husband.” According to its Goodreads description, the 14-page story follows “an ugly girl who was short and dumpy, had one leg a bit shorter than the other, and her eyebrows met in the middle” — and she “wanted to marry.”
“Who will marry her while all the people made fun of her?” the premise asks. “Then, she married the wicker husband. what happened when she married him? What was the people’s reaction?”
In 2020, the story was turned into a folk musical that ran for a few weeks at the Watermill Theatre in Newbury, England.

A Facebook post from the theatre in March 2020 revealed that the production would use puppetry to bring the wicker man to life. “It is these puppets that steal the show,” recaps The Guardian’s three-star review of the show.
How Are Fans Reacting to the Trailer?
Fans’ reactions to the trailer have ranged from humorous posts about the plot to pure confusion to ... well, thirst with a side helping of surprise.
Beneath the YouTube trailer, fans left comments poking fun at the concept.
“Expected a horror film trailer, stayed for whatever this was,” one joked.
Another wrote, “Just when I think Alexander Skarsgard has finally achieved his weirdest role he comes at me with this.”
A third said, “I love that Peter Dinklage’s character is asked to make a Cottagecore Frankenstein and immediately says ‘say less.’”
Ikea joined in on the fun on Instagram by sharing a picture of a chair made of wicker with text that read “husband material.”
“We’ve got plenty of husband material,” the furniture company captioned the post before asking social media users to share how many times they watched the “Wicker” trailer.
A “Wicker” movie account responded, “No assembly required.”
To which Ikea cheekily replied, “Looking at our wicker furniture a little differently these days,” with a smirk emoji.
One Instagram user commented with an idea for the store. “And now all wicker items must be renamed to Skarsgård,” she wrote.
“Big Wick Energy,” another comment read.
Content creator JessAfterDark shared a hilarious Instagram video of her watching the trailer with her husband, who uttered, “Oh God!” when he saw Skarsgård’s character for the first time.
When the clip ended, he said he “couldn’t wait” to watch the movie.
Another Instagram user predicted that “baskets are about to make a huge comeback” on her page, adding “iykyk” (if you know you know).
In the caption she playfully wrote, “Alex Skarsgård… the basket that you are.”

title: A Hospital Patient Dreamed Of Attending A Metal Concert. So The Show Came To Him
summary: Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert but couldn’t leave the facility. So the show came to him.
story: Now *this* is metal.

Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert after receiving some difficult news about his health, clinical chaplain Roshene Lawson tells TODAY.com. While he was too medically fragile to leave the facility, Lawson pulled some strings to make magic happen.

With the help of staff and some kind folks at a local venue, Lawson threw a real metal show at the hospital in July, featuring band The Scepter, a whole lot of headbanging and, of course, that metalhead spirit.
Berry was able to rock out safely.

“Our clinical manager had told me he had some tears coming down during the concert,” Lawson says of Berry. “I went to ask him after. I said, ‘Were you crying because it was so loud?’ ... and he laughed and he said, ‘No, I’m really happy.’”

The Scepter played a 40-minute set for Berry, Lawson recounts. The band performed while fully decked out in their metal garb. They also set up their lights and blaring amps, along with some fans to blast their long locks, she says.
The Scepter’s Josh Collins explains that the band attempted to give Berry the most authentic experience they could.

“We wanted to give him a real show, not a watered down version because we were playing in a hospital,” he says. “It was emotional, for sure, but mostly we just felt privileged to be there and to play for him.”
Nurses painted Berry’s nails for the occasion and dressed him in a heavy metal shirt, Lawson adds. She even made tickets for the event, which patients used to attend the rock show.
“Everybody had to have their ticket to get in, and we tore the ticket, and they came in, and we had staff enjoying it with them,” Lawson says.

The chaplain explains that the idea for the concert came from a conversation she had with Berry after he was told about a change in his condition. She declined to disclose further medical details to protect Berry’s privacy.

“I went in and said to him, ‘Really, we can focus on this and how sad and frustrating it is, or we can focus on what you want to do with what’s left of life,’” Lawson recalls. “And he said, ‘I’d really, really like to go to a heavy metal concert.’”

Since Berry wasn’t cleared to leave the hospital, Lawson had to get creative. She called around and found Dominion Tavern, a spot that regularly hosts shows, and asked them for help. The business was more than happy to get on board, owner Scott McClinton says.
“I was in the unique position to be able to pull something like this off,” McClinton says. “I had most of the equipment, I know tons of bands and put on multiple shows weekly.”
It didn’t take long for McClinton to tap local band The Scepter for the performance, he says.

“They play straight-up epic, fun metal and always put on a great show,” McClinton says. “Plus I know a few of the members pretty well and they’re just really great, sweet dudes who I knew would say yes immediately – which was key as we didn’t have much time to organize all this.”
One of the trickiest aspects of the planning process, Lawson says, was finding the right spot to host such a raucous bash.

“It’s not quiet music, and we have other patients for whom that might not be their genre of music, so we had to find a place where we could put a proper concert on, where he could really live it as a concert,” Lawson says.
A conference room ended up being the perfect venue. And after moving around some furniture and setting up the band’s equipment, the scene was transformed, Lawson says.
“And honestly, the nurses, the recreation therapists, the physio, the OT, the clinical manager — everybody worked together to make this a fun thing for him,” Lawson adds.

While heavy metal isn’t always associated with comfort and peace, Lawson explains that it’s critical to meet patients’ unique needs. It’s especially important in a medical environment where there isn’t a lot of room to scream and shout and let it all out when you need to, she says.

“You and I could go home to our place, and if we’re having a bad day, just scream into a pillow or cry out loud or do whatever we need to do,” Lawson explains. “That’s harder to do when you’re in care.”

Lawson said that having a moment to rock out is “so cathartic, when you can really let that noise wash over you and it’s not the buzzing of the machines or the ringing of the call bells or the sound of the suction machine. It is bona fide living.”
The experience wasn’t just a memorable one for Berry. It’s also been impactful for McClinton, Lawson and all those involved.
“Getting to see Tim’s smile and the reaction from the staff is something that will stay with me for the rest of my life,” McClinton says.
He adds that “if you get a chance to help make someone’s day better, just do it.”
“It’ll be great for them and could be unbelievably rewarding for you,”  McClinton says.
The Scepter, whose members say they’ve felt moved by the concert as well, is also dedicating their next album to Berry.

“He brought us into something much bigger than we ever expected, and it feels right that he should be part of what comes next for us,” Collins says. “Dedicating the album to Tim is our way of recognizing him and what this experience has meant to the band.”
Rock on, Tim. Rock on.

title: Former Marine held in Russia for more than 4 years is back in the U.S.
summary: Former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman released from jail in Russia
story: A former U.S. Marine who spent more than four years in a Russian prison and is believed to be seriously ill was back in the United States Tuesday night, a White House official said.
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff said on X that he had the “profound privilege” of welcoming Robert Gilman, 32, home. He praised President Donald Trump for his release.
“He can now finally return to his family and receive the medical care he needs,” Witkoff said.
Trump earlier announced the release on Truth Social, saying Gilman was freed after he discussed the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said Gilman, a teacher, was released “very much on a Humanitarian Basis,” with no exchange of prisoners having taken place. He was expected to land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C.
The president added in his post that he had spoken to Gilman “and he had one request — A GREAT cheeseburger when he lands. I will take care of that!”
The Russian government has not commented on the release.

About 50 days ago, Gilman was diagnosed with a “dissociative stupor — a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat,” Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., said in a statement following the man’s release.

“He was essentially catatonic and also suffered a severe case of pneumonia,” added Markey, who has been campaigning for Gilman’s release. “We don’t yet know the full details of his current condition or the long-term impact on his recovery.”
Gilman’s sister Lexie Hudson thanked Trump in a statement issued by Global Reach, an advocacy group representing his family.
“There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action,” she said.
“I am looking forward to seeing Robert. I haven’t been able to speak with him once since this all began,” she added. “We will make sure that he gets the treatment and support that he needs.”

Before his release, Hudson said in a statement Sunday that she was worried that he would die if he wasn’t freed. “I’m more afraid for my brother than I have been since this horrible nightmare started,” she said in the statement issued by Global Reach.

Her comments Sunday came around a month after Russia’s Kommersant newspaper reported that Gilman had been ​admitted to a hospital. Quoting his lawyer Irina Brazhnikova, the business daily reported that he was receiving treatment but it was too early to talk about a diagnosis.

Gilman, who served in the Marines from August 2019 until August 2020, had been detained in 2022. He was initially handed a 3 ½-year sentence for beating a police officer after being taken off a train for causing a disturbance.

While serving his sentence, Gilman was accused in October 2024 of attacking a prison inspector during a cell check, beating an investigator and assaulting a guard; he was sentenced to eight years and one month.
Last year, his sentence was extended again to 10 years after he was found guilty of assaulting prison guards.
Gilman’s American supporters contend he was ill when he was first arrested and also that he was provoked while in prison into actions that led to further charges.
According to Markey, Gilman was “subjected to physical torture, forced medication, and provocations by Russian authorities” throughout his detention.
“There is no doubt that his treatment by Russian authorities is the reason Robert is in this precarious state today,” he added.
Gilman was one of at least 10 Americans known to be imprisoned in Russia.

title: More than 160 people killed in Colombia’s strongest earthquake in years
summary: At least 132 people were killed Monday in a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that shook western Colombia, collapsing hospitals, schools and other buildings and leaving people trapped under the rubble.
story: At least 169 people were killed Monday in a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that shook western Colombia, collapsing hospitals, schools and other buildings and leaving people trapped under the rubble.

The worst-hit cities include Pereira, Cali, Quibdó, Manizales and Armenia, all of which remain under “red alert,” the nation’s highest-level disaster threat level, according to Colombia’s nonprofit Association of Capital Cities, which provided the death toll.
Seven airports have suspended operations, and hospitals, roads, transportation, aqueducts, energy and telecommunications have been disrupted in the areas hardest hit, it said.
Colombia’s newly inaugurated president, Abelardo De La Espriella, said in a national briefing that 700 people were injured in the temblor and an estimated 5,000 homes were damaged or destroyed.

title: ‘A piece of our history’: Untouched Roman shipwreck discovered off Italy
summary: Divers have uncovered a Roman-era shipwreck that had remained untouched on the seabed off Sicily for more than 2,000 years, police on the Mediterranean island said.
story: Divers have uncovered a Roman-era shipwreck that had remained untouched on the seabed off Sicily for more than 2,000 years, police on the Mediterranean island said.

Italian Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli described it on social media as “one of the most significant underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years,” with experts dating the vessel back to the first or second century B.C.

“The sea continues to reveal precious evidence of our history,” Giuli said. “This shipwreck tells the story of the people, trade routes, and exchanges that made the Mediterranean a crossroads of civilizations.”
After a tipoff from residents, the ship was discovered by divers  around 3 miles off Sicily’s western coast and about 150 feet below the surface, Italian authorities said in a statement.

title: Iran sets steep demands to reopen Hormuz despite hopes Oman deal could break impasse
summary: Tehran has vowed not to reopen the shipping lane “until America corrects its behavior,” despite a looming agreement with Oman.
story: There are no ongoing negotiations between Tehran and Washington, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday, after Tehran set out a steep series of demands for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
“The intermediaries are still making efforts to find ways to resume negotiations,” Araghchi said.

He tempered optimism stirred by Iran’s separate discussions with Oman over the future management of the waterway, saying that “changes to maritime routes in the Strait of Hormuz are a technical and legal matter and do not mean that the Strait of Hormuz has been reopened.”

Araghchi’s statement came a day after top Iranian security official Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr laid out the country’s conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, saying it would not do so “until America corrects its behavior.”

The statement from Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary, as carried by Iranian state media, stated that the U.S. must withdraw its naval blockade, pay Iran damages for the war, unfreeze Iranian assets, lift sanctions on Tehran and permanently end the conflict against Iran and its regional allies.
Even though the demands are steep, analysts say they are still largely within the framework of the initial deal the two sides reached in June.

“The Supreme National Security Council of Iran, which is really a consensus body, they have come to a realization that for them the best route is returning back to the MOU,” Mehran Haghirian, director of research and programs at the Bourse & Bazaar Foundation London-based think tank, said in a phone interview.
“They want to make sure that they get some of those things up-front, or at least there is a process for them before there is any movement on Hormuz.”
The U.S. has yet to respond publicly to the list of conditions. Top officials have previously ruled out making any immediate payments to Iran during past efforts to seal a deal to end the war.

The country’s enriched uranium stockpile has also been a sticking point for Washington, which insists Iran must abandon its nuclear ambitions. The stalled negotiations have left the Strait of Hormuz largely impassable for months, save for brief periods of operation. Thousands of sailors remain stranded in the region, unable to return home or keep the world’s supply of oil flowing.

“What we’re really working through now is how you can actually set up a traffic scheme so that the ships that pass can pass through safely,” Vice President JD Vance told Fox News on Saturday. That scheme, Vance said, would include demining efforts and also assurances from Tehran that it would not fire on transiting vessels.

On Saturday, Oman condemned attacks on the vessels that were attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, saying in a statement that such attacks could affect its negotiations with Iran over the waterway’s management. The UAE and Kuwait on Saturday also condemned an Iranian missile attack on an Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. tanker.
Oman nonetheless said its discussions with Iran were “proceeding in a positive and constructive atmosphere.”

Iran and Oman, neighbors across the Strait of Hormuz, have been negotiating an agreement on how to manage traffic through the waterway, including considerations of a toll fee. The discussions have also been viewed optimistically, raising hopes that they could finally lead to reopening the strait.
But Iranian officials have dismissed any such possibility. Iran’s discussions with Oman do “not mean the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz,” Araghchi said Saturday.

Even though the Iranian officials say the discussions don’t mean an immediate reopening of Hormuz, Haghirian said the discussions would lay critical groundwork for if and when Iran reaches an agreement with the U.S. over Hormuz.

Iranian state media on Sunday reported that President Masoud Pezeshkian had met with the country’s absent Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, discussing “the war and the future ahead.” No evidence was provided that the meeting took place.

Pezeshkian earlier this week said that it had been “very difficult” to contact the 56-year-old leader, who has not been seen publicly since he was badly injured in the U.S. strikes that killed his father.
Meanwhile, the Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen again attacked Saudi Arabia on Sunday, with Yemen’s news agency saying the forces targeted the Mocha port along the Red Sea.

The Houthis have launched several attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent days, also hitting a Saudi Aramco oil refinery in the port city of Jizan with a drone. It said Sunday that the attack on the refinery was in response to Saudi drones’ incursions into the Saada and Hajjah airspaces of Yemen.
The Saudi Energy Ministry said Sunday on X that the fire that broke out at the refinery had been extinguished and nobody was injured.

The world’s top oil exporter, Aramco, is seeking to reroute some of its exports to the Red Sea instead of the Persian Gulf in an effort to circumvent the shuttered Strait of Hormuz. Riyadh on Saturday condemned the attacks by the Houthis, who it said had attacked the kingdom since July 13 and shipping vessels since July 22.

title: Israel rejects Trump’s 15-point plan for Gaza
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ⁠said Israeli forces wouldn’t withdraw from the war-torn enclave until Hamas fully disarms
story: Israel will not accept the 15-point plan for Gaza set out by President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Sunday.

“I want to clarify this: Israel rejects the 15-point document. I have heard people saying, ‘You didn’t say that.’ So here I am saying it again,” he told a Cabinet meeting, referring to the peace plan set out by Trump last year. “The IDF will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed,” he added.
Trump last month touted a breakthrough in his Gaza peace plan, saying that Hamas has agreed to lay down arms.

The peace plan called for a phased withdrawal of Israel’s troops from Gaza alongside the disarmament of Hamas, but Netanyahu said Israeli forces are not going anywhere until Hamas completely disarms first.
“When I say Hamas must be disarmed, I mean heavy weapons, lighter weapons, all weapons. We are talking about genuine disarmament, not a fictitious one,” Netanyahu said Sunday.

Hamas had last month said that it would disarm, but only after Israel withdraws completely and stops all hostilities. The group also said that laying down its heavy weapons would come later in the process, conditional on the establishment of a Palestinian state.

Netanyahu, meanwhile, reaffirmed that “as long as I am prime minister, there will be no Palestinian state.” The leader is currently facing a domestic political battle for survival ahead of elections set for October, with the status of the Gaza and Iran wars likely to prove pivotal.

The explicit rejection of the peace plan, frequently touted by Trump as a key foreign policy achievement, also comes after months of growing tensions between the White House and Israel’s leadership over Iran. The White House did not immediately comment on the remarks.

Netanyahu said of Washington: “We are currently discussing this issue with the Americans. They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand firm on these matters.”

The Israeli leader may consider it worthwhile to “enter a new confrontation with President Trump,” said Ronni Shaked, a research fellow at the Harry S. Truman Institute at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, as his own popularity wanes ahead of October’s election.

“After three years, he is without any victory, and he just wants to show now to the people of Israel, before the election, that look at me, I have victory, and the victory is that we are going to disarm Hamas,” Shaked said in a phone interview, referring to the tactic as an “illusion.”

Responding to Netanyahu’s statement Sunday, senior Hamas official Basim Naeem said that the group expects the mediators and the U.S. to “exert pressure” on Netanyahu and his government to abide by the road map and “prevent him from obstructing the process for domestic political and electoral considerations.”

A further Hamas statement reaffirmed its commitment to the agreed-upon road map, reiterating the group’s “seriousness in engaging responsibly in implementing the fifteen points agreed upon and establishing a clear timetable for their implementation.”

Mohammad Dahlan, a member of the Palestinian Legislative Council, said Netanyahu’s announcement “represents a challenge, contempt, and deception of the American administration and President Trump’s team,” adding that Washington “now realizes that Netanyahu is an obstacle to achieving security and stability.”

Netanyahu’s far-right finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, welcomed his announcement after seeking to pressure the leader into a more hard-line stance. “I congratulate the Prime Minister for responding to our demand and clarifying unequivocally,” he said on X.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, meanwhile, “emphasized the necessity for all parties to fulfill their commitments and refrain from taking any actions that could hinder the implementation process or undermine the progress achieved,” his office said in a statement.

Add NBC News to Google

Despite agreeing to halt attacks in October, Israel has continued its deadly strikes on the Palestinian enclave. On Saturday, recovery operations concluded at the Karam Building in Gaza after 19 bodies were found under the rubble, according to the Gaza civil defense. Israel and Hamas both regularly accuse the other of breaching the ceasefire.

More than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Oct. 7, 2023, according to the enclave’s health officials, including more than 1,200 people since the ceasefire began in October. Israel launched its war in Gaza in response to the Hamas-led attack in which around 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
